children.title: Paired-Request Structure
children.top_down_role: One-to-one transportation requests linking a specific origin to a specific destination.

knowledge_statements.title: Paired-Request Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines paired pickup-and-delivery requests independently of precedence and vehicle-assignment rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite set of service vertices. A paired-request instance is a finite set \(\mathcal R\) together with maps \(p,d:\mathcal R\to V\) and quantities \(q:\mathcal R\to\mathbb R_{>0}\), where \(p(r)\ne d(r)\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\). Request \(r\) requires collection of \(q(r)\) units at its pickup vertex \(p(r)\) and delivery of those same units at its associated delivery vertex \(d(r)\). The pairing is retained even when several requests share a service vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each request links one pickup vertex to one distinct delivery vertex and specifies a positive quantity whose identity is preserved between the two services.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(\mathcal R\) are finite.
\(q(r)>0\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\mapsto (p(r),d(r),q(r))\) defines the paired-request structure.

notation.meaning: pickup and delivery vertices of request r
positive quantity associated with request r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard paired pickup-and-delivery request definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no vehicle-routing source or inspectable locator supports the precise paired-request formulation.

children.title: Pickup-Before-Delivery Precedence
children.top_down_role: Visit-order restrictions associated with paired transportation requests.

knowledge_statements.title: Pickup-Before-Delivery Precedence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States temporal precedence for each paired request, without imposing same-vehicle service.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each request \(r\in\mathcal R\), let \(t_p(r)\) and \(t_d(r)\) be the service-start times at its pickup and delivery occurrences. Pickup-before-delivery precedence holds precisely when \[t_p(r)+s_p(r)\le t_d(r)\qquad\text{for every }r\in\mathcal R,\] where \(s_p(r)\ge0\) is the pickup service duration. Thus delivery may begin only after pickup service has finished; equality permits immediate delivery when travel and waiting time are zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every request’s delivery service must start no earlier than completion of its pickup service.
assumptions_latex: Each request has identified pickup and delivery service occurrences.
All service times are measured on a common time scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_p(r)+s_p(r)\le t_d(r)\) for all \(r\in\mathcal R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and matches the leaf, but the exact service-completion precedence convention requires an applicable source with a specific locator.

children.title: Same-Vehicle Request Service
children.top_down_role: Vehicle-coupling requirements for servicing both locations of a request.

knowledge_statements.title: Same-Vehicle Request Service
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines nontransferable service of a paired request by a single vehicle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the fleet and let \(a_p,a_d:\mathcal R\to K\) assign the pickup and delivery occurrences of every served request to vehicles. Same-vehicle request service holds precisely when \[a_p(r)=a_d(r)\qquad\text{for every }r\in\mathcal R.\] Equivalently, if \(x^p_{rk}\) and \(x^d_{rk}\) indicate service of the two occurrences by vehicle \(k\), then \(x^p_{rk}=x^d_{rk}\) for all \(r\in\mathcal R\) and \(k\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vehicle collecting a request must also perform its associated delivery, so transfer between vehicles is forbidden.
assumptions_latex: Every pickup and delivery occurrence is assigned to exactly one vehicle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_p(r)=a_d(r)\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\).

notation.meaning: vehicles assigned to the pickup and delivery of request r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The same-vehicle condition and its indicator formulation are coherent under the stated unique-assignment assumption, but neither is supported by a cited source.

children.title: Customer-to-Depot Collection
children.top_down_role: Routing structures that consolidate goods or requests from multiple customers at a depot.

knowledge_statements.title: Customer-to-Depot Collection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the collection-only capacitated routing regime with a common depot destination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\) be a depot, \(C\) a finite customer set, \(q_i>0\) the quantity collected at customer \(i\), and \(Q>0\) the vehicle capacity. A customer-to-depot collection route begins at \(0\) with load \(L_0=0\), visits assigned customers, increases its load by \(q_i\) immediately after visiting \(i\), and returns to \(0\), where the collected load is unloaded. Feasibility requires \(0\le L\le Q\) throughout the route and service of every customer exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vehicles leave the depot empty, collect positive quantities from customers, respect capacity, and return the collected material to the depot.
assumptions_latex: All collected quantities have the depot as their destination.
Each vehicle has capacity \(Q>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_i^+=L_i^-+q_i\) and \(0\le L_i^+\le Q\) at every visited customer \(i\).

notation.meaning: vehicle loads immediately before and after service at i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The collection-only definition fits the container, but its capacity, route, and exactly-once conventions have no supporting vehicle-routing citation.

children.title: Depot-to-Customer Distribution
children.top_down_role: Routing structures distributing depot-originating goods or requests to multiple customers.

knowledge_statements.title: Depot-to-Customer Distribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the distribution-only capacitated routing regime with a common depot origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\) be a depot, \(C\) a finite customer set, \(d_i>0\) the quantity required by customer \(i\), and \(Q>0\) the vehicle capacity. A depot-to-customer distribution route leaves \(0\) carrying the total demand assigned to that route, visits its assigned customers, and decreases its load by \(d_i\) immediately after serving customer \(i\). Feasibility requires an initial load at most \(Q\), nonnegative load throughout the route, and service of every customer exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vehicles load customer orders at the depot, deliver them along capacity-feasible routes, and serve every customer once.
assumptions_latex: All delivered quantities originate at the depot.
Each vehicle has capacity \(Q>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_i^+=L_i^--d_i\) and \(0\le L_i^+\le L_i^-\le Q\) at every visited customer \(i\).

notation.meaning: vehicle loads immediately before and after service at i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distribution-only definition is internally consistent and locally appropriate, but no cited source supports the selected routing and service conventions.

children.title: Combined Collection–Distribution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Planning settings containing both depot-centered collection and distribution traffic.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Collection–Distribution Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines routes carrying both depot-origin deliveries and depot-destination collections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each customer \(i\in C\) have a delivery quantity \(d_i\ge0\) and a collection quantity \(p_i\ge0\), not both zero. In a combined collection–distribution regime, a vehicle leaves the depot with its assigned delivery load, serves its customers according to the regime's permitted visit pattern, and returns collected material to the depot. At a service of \(i\), the load satisfies \[L_i^+=L_i^- - d_i+p_i,\qquad L_i^-\ge d_i,\qquad 0\le L_i^+\le Q.\] Additional ordering or simultaneity rules distinguish particular subfamilies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routes jointly deliver depot-origin goods and collect depot-bound goods while satisfying the corresponding load transition and capacity constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each customer has at least one positive transfer quantity.
Delivered goods originate and collected goods terminate at the common depot.
Vehicle capacity is \(Q>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_i^+=L_i^- - d_i+p_i\) with \(L_i^-\ge d_i\) and \(0\le L_i^+\le Q\).

notation.meaning: delivery and collection quantities at customer i
loads immediately before and after service at i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard mixed collection-and-distribution load model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Combined collection–distribution families differ over single versus separate visits and ordering rules. The stated per-service transition may be valid for some variants, but its intended breadth cannot be established without a specific source.

children.title: Many-to-Many Request Networks
children.top_down_role: Transportation request systems with multiple origins and multiple destinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Many-to-Many Request Networks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines transport demand between arbitrary ordered pairs of service vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a finite service network and let \(q_{uv}\ge0\) denote demand transported from \(u\) to \(v\) for distinct vertices \(u,v\in V\). A many-to-many request network permits positive demand on arbitrary ordered pairs, so neither all origins nor all destinations need coincide with a depot. Its active request set is \[\mathcal R=\{(u,v)\in V\times V:u\ne v,\ q_{uv}>0\}.\] A routing solution must arrange vehicle movements and service decisions that transport every active quantity from its specified origin to its specified destination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive transport requests may connect arbitrary distinct network vertices; no single depot must be the common origin or destination.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
Every active demand quantity is nonnegative and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R\subseteq\{(u,v)\in V\times V:u\ne v\}\) may contain multiple origins and multiple destinations.

notation.meaning: quantity requested from u to v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The many-to-many demand definition fits the leaf, but no cited routing source supports the exact demand-matrix and mandatory-transport formulation.

children.title: Commodity-Transfer Structure
children.top_down_role: Movement patterns for commodities or loads across many-to-many request networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Commodity-Transfer Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents each commodity by origin-destination balance equations on a routing network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a directed network and \(H\) a finite commodity set. Commodity \(h\in H\) has origin \(o_h\), destination \(d_h\ne o_h\), and quantity \(q_h>0\). For arc-transfer variables \(f_a^h\ge0\), conservation is represented by \[\sum_{a\in\delta^+(v)}f_a^h-\sum_{a\in\delta^-(v)}f_a^h=\begin{cases}q_h,&v=o_h,\\-q_h,&v=d_h,\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\] If routed arc capacity is \(U_a\), feasibility additionally requires \(\sum_{h\in H}f_a^h\le U_a\) for every \(a\in A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each commodity has an origin, destination, and quantity represented by flow conservation, with aggregate commodity flow respecting routed capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) and \(H\) are finite.
Commodity transfer may be represented as nonnegative arc flow.
Each routed arc has capacity \(U_a\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Commodity balances hold at every vertex and \(\sum_{h\in H}f_a^h\le U_a\) on every arc.

notation.meaning: flow of commodity h on arc a
origin, destination, and quantity of commodity h
available routed capacity on arc a

review_flags: vehicle-routing interpretation and applicable source require review

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multicommodity balance equations are standard, but the meaning of routed arc capacity and the representation's applicability to this vehicle-routing taxonomy require a specific supporting source.

children.title: Request-Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Direct, transferable, splittable, or vehicle-specific service relationships among requests.

knowledge_statements.title: Request-Coupling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies how strongly pickup and delivery decisions retain request identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each paired request \(r\), let \(P_r\) and \(D_r\) denote its pickup and delivery occurrences, with service times \(t(P_r),t(D_r)\) and vehicle labels \(a(P_r),a(D_r)\). A request-coupling regime specifies which links are enforced: aggregate uncoupled service retains only vertex-level balances; transferable paired service retains the association and requires \(t(P_r)\le t(D_r)\); nontransferable paired service additionally requires \(a(P_r)=a(D_r)\). Further resource or ride-time constraints may strengthen, but do not weaken, the selected regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling ranges from aggregate balance only, through paired transferable service, to paired service whose pickup and delivery use the same vehicle.
assumptions_latex: Every paired request has identifiable pickup and delivery occurrences.
Service times share a common ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupling regime is determined by whether pairing, precedence, and \(a(P_r)=a(D_r)\) are enforced.

notation.meaning: pickup and delivery occurrences of request r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coupling levels formalize common request-transfer distinctions
taxonomy boundaries vary across vehicle-routing literature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed coupling hierarchy is plausible but not a universally fixed classification. A source is needed to establish the levels, the role of precedence, and the transferable/nontransferable terminology.

children.title: Backhaul Routing
children.top_down_role: Routing structures separating or sequencing linehaul deliveries and return pickups.

knowledge_statements.title: Backhaul Routing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the classical linehaul-before-backhaul convention for each depot route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let customers be partitioned into linehaul customers \(L\), receiving deliveries from depot \(0\), and backhaul customers \(B\), supplying collections for depot \(0\). A classical backhaul route starts and ends at \(0\), serves assigned customers, respects vehicle capacity, and satisfies the ordering rule that every visited linehaul precedes every visited backhaul. For a route sequence \((v_1,\ldots,v_m)\), this means \[v_i\in B,\ j>i\ \Longrightarrow\ v_j\notin L.\] Every customer is assigned to exactly one route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each depot route completes all assigned deliveries before beginning its assigned collections, while respecting capacity and unique customer service.
assumptions_latex: \(L\cap B=\varnothing\).
Linehaul goods originate and backhaul goods terminate at the depot.
Vehicles have finite capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No linehaul customer occurs after a backhaul customer on the same route.

notation.meaning: ordered customer sequence of one route

review_flags: some literature permits mixed ordering, so the classical convention is stated explicitly

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record explicitly chooses the classical linehaul-before-backhaul variant and otherwise fits the leaf, but that convention needs an authoritative vehicle-routing citation with a precise locator.

children.title: Simultaneous Pickup–Delivery Routing
children.top_down_role: Routing structures allowing pickup and delivery service at the same customer visit.

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Pickup–Delivery Routing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines one-visit service with both delivery and pickup at each customer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each customer \(i\in C\) require delivery \(d_i\ge0\) from depot \(0\) and pickup \(p_i\ge0\) for return to \(0\), with \(d_i+p_i>0\). In simultaneous pickup–delivery routing, both transfers at \(i\) are completed during the same vehicle visit. If \(L_i^-\) and \(L_i^+\) are loads immediately before and after service, then \[L_i^+=L_i^- - d_i+p_i,\qquad L_i^-\ge d_i,\qquad 0\le L_i^+\le Q.\] Each customer is visited exactly once by one depot route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single visit to each customer performs both its delivery and pickup, with the resulting vehicle load remaining feasible.
assumptions_latex: All transfers are between customers and the common depot.
Vehicle capacity is \(Q>0\).
Each customer has a positive delivery or pickup quantity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both transfers occur in one visit and satisfy \(L_i^+=L_i^- - d_i+p_i\) within capacity.

notation.meaning: delivery and pickup quantities at customer i
loads before and after simultaneous service

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard simultaneous pickup-and-delivery routing definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-visit simultaneous pickup–delivery definition and load transition are coherent, but no cited source supports the exact model conventions.

children.title: Mixed Backhaul–Simultaneous Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instances combining sequenced backhaul customers with simultaneous-service customers.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Backhaul–Simultaneous Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines hybrid instances containing pure linehauls, pure backhauls, and simultaneous-service customers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let customers be partitioned into \(L=\{i:d_i>0,\ p_i=0\}\), \(B=\{i:d_i=0,\ p_i>0\}\), and \(S=\{i:d_i>0,\ p_i>0\}\). A mixed backhaul–simultaneous regime serves every customer once, performs both transfers in the single visit to each \(i\in S\), and requires pure linehaul customers to precede pure backhaul customers on each route. Every service obeys \[L_i^+=L_i^- - d_i+p_i,\qquad L_i^-\ge d_i,\qquad 0\le L_i^+\le Q.\] The placement of customers in \(S\) is governed by the chosen hybrid variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routes combine pure deliveries, pure collections, and one-visit simultaneous customers while retaining linehaul-before-backhaul ordering for the pure classes.
assumptions_latex: All customer transfers use a common depot.
Vehicle capacity is \(Q>0\).
Each customer belongs to exactly one of \(L\), \(B\), or \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pure linehauls precede pure backhauls, simultaneous customers receive one-visit service, and all load transitions remain feasible.

notation.meaning: pure linehaul, pure backhaul, and simultaneous customer sets
delivery and pickup quantities at customer i
vehicle loads before and after customer service

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit hybridization of backhaul and simultaneous-service constraints
hybrid variants differ on placement of simultaneous customers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hybrid regime is not standardized, and the admissible placement of simultaneous-service customers is left variant-dependent. A specific source is required before its mathematical definition can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Dial-a-Ride Problems
children.top_down_role: Demand-responsive passenger routing with individual transportation requests.

assumptions_latex: A directed travel network \(G=(V,A)\) has nonnegative travel costs and times.
Each request \(i\in R\) has pickup node \(p_i\), delivery node \(d_i\), demand \(q_i\), and service data.
A fleet \(K\) has vehicle capacities \(Q_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible solution is a collection of vehicle routes satisfying all stated pairing, precedence, timing, ride-time, and capacity constraints; an optimum minimizes the prescribed fleet-routing objective.

notation.meaning: pickup and delivery nodes of request i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static many-to-many dial-a-ride formulation with paired passenger requests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dial-a-ride problem consists of requests \(R\) and vehicles \(K\). Each request \(i\in R\) must be assigned to one vehicle whose route visits \(p_i\) before \(d_i\). If service starts at times \(B_{p_i}\) and \(B_{d_i}\), then applicable time windows must hold, the ride time \(B_{d_i}-B_{p_i}-s_{p_i}\) must not exceed its prescribed limit, and the load after every visit must lie between zero and the assigned vehicle's capacity. Every request is served exactly once, and routes begin and end at their specified depots. The objective commonly minimizes routing cost, fleet use, passenger inconvenience, or a stated combination thereof.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dial-a-ride routing assigns every paired passenger pickup and delivery to one vehicle, preserving pickup precedence while satisfying time, ride-time, depot, and capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Dial-a-Ride Problems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and its content kind fit the Dial-a-Ride Problems leaf, and the paired pickup-delivery, precedence, ride-time, and capacity description is mathematically plausible. However, no source reference or inspectable locator is supplied, so the formulation and claimed range of objectives cannot be evidence-checked.

children.title: Passenger-Service Routing
children.top_down_role: Broader routing settings shaped by passenger service quality and operating policies.

assumptions_latex: A directed network \(G=(V,A)\) and a fleet \(K\) are given.
Each passenger request specifies admissible boarding and alighting service.
All operational constraints and the objective are part of the instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible passenger-service plan assigns and sequences all accepted passenger services on vehicle routes while satisfying the declared operational and service-quality constraints.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General passenger-routing model, including but not restricted to paired door-to-door requests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Passenger-service routing is the optimization problem of selecting, assigning, and sequencing passenger services on routes operated by vehicles \(K\) over \(G=(V,A)\). For each accepted request \(i\in R\), the route must realize its specified boarding and alighting pattern and satisfy the instance's temporal, vehicle-compatibility, accessibility, capacity, and service-quality constraints. A feasible solution also respects route origins, destinations, and operating horizons. The objective is an explicitly stated function of operating cost, rejected demand, waiting, transfers, travel time, or other service measures; no particular combination is intrinsic to the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passenger-service routing assigns passenger movements to vehicle routes subject to the instance's operational and service-quality rules and optimizes a stated cost or service objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Passenger-Service Routing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate content kind for this leaf, but the proposed category is intentionally broader than dial-a-ride and includes boarding patterns, transfers, accessibility, rejection, and varied service objectives. With no cited source or locator, the exact scope of Passenger-Service Routing cannot be established reliably.

children.title: Ride-Time Service Constraints
children.top_down_role: Passenger-facing limits involving in-vehicle time, waiting, detours, or service timing.

assumptions_latex: Request \(i\) is picked up at \(p_i\) and delivered at \(d_i\).
Service begins at times \(B_v\), and service at \(p_i\) lasts \(s_{p_i}\).
The maximum permitted in-vehicle time is \(L_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Request \(i\) satisfies its ride-time requirement exactly when \(0\le B_{d_i}-B_{p_i}-s_{p_i}\le L_i\).

notation.meaning: maximum ride time for request i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ride time excludes pickup service and ends when delivery service begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every served request \(i\), define its in-vehicle ride time by \(T_i^{\mathrm{ride}}=B_{d_i}-B_{p_i}-s_{p_i}\). The ride-time service constraint is
\[
0\le T_i^{\mathrm{ride}}\le L_i.
\]
If service quality is expressed relative to direct travel time \(t_{p_i d_i}\), an alternative admissible bound is \(T_i^{\mathrm{ride}}\le \alpha_i t_{p_i d_i}+\beta_i\), where \(\alpha_i\ge 1\) and \(\beta_i\ge 0\) are specified. The chosen absolute or relative convention must be fixed by the instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A passenger's elapsed in-vehicle time, from completion of pickup service to the start of delivery service, may not exceed the specified absolute or relative limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Ride-Time Service Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for this constraint leaf, and the absolute ride-time formula is internally consistent with the stated service-start convention. A source is still required to support that convention and the asserted affine relative bound involving alpha_i and beta_i.

children.title: Passenger-Capacity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Vehicle occupancy and request-compatibility structures in passenger routing.

assumptions_latex: Each pickup request \(i\) adds demand \(q_i>0\), and its delivery removes the same demand.
Vehicle \(k\) has capacity \(Q_k>0\).
Loads are measured immediately after service at each visited node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Capacity feasibility requires \(0\le y_{kj}\le Q_k\) after every visit \(j\) on vehicle \(k\)'s route.

notation.meaning: load after the j-th visit of vehicle k

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies passenger capacity by whether capacities vary across vehicles or are nonbinding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Along a route of vehicle \(k\), initialize \(y_{k0}=0\) and update the load by \(y_{kj}=y_{k,j-1}+q_i\) after pickup \(p_i\), by \(y_{kj}=y_{k,j-1}-q_i\) after delivery \(d_i\), and by no change at other visits. Capacity feasibility is \(0\le y_{kj}\le Q_k\) for every visit \(j\). The regime is homogeneous-capacitated when all finite \(Q_k\) are equal, heterogeneous-capacitated when they may differ, and uncapacitated when every \(Q_k\) is at least the total simultaneously transportable demand, making the upper bounds redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passenger loads increase at pickups and decrease at deliveries. Homogeneous, heterogeneous, and effectively uncapacitated regimes differ according to the vehicle capacity values.
knowledge_statements.title: Passenger-Capacity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the Passenger-Capacity Regimes leaf, and the load recursion is coherent. No source supports the homogeneous, heterogeneous, and uncapacitated classification or the particular criterion stated for redundancy of capacity bounds.

children.title: Loading-Constrained Routing
children.top_down_role: Routing settings shaped by packing, stacking, accessibility, or load-arrangement restrictions.

assumptions_latex: Each request \(i\) has a physical item with declared dimensions, weight, and handling rules.
Vehicle \(k\) has a specified loading space \(S_k\).
Route service order determines when each item enters and leaves the loading space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A route is loading-feasible exactly when every carried-item set admits placements satisfying containment, nonoverlap, and all declared handling constraints throughout the route.

notation.meaning: items aboard after route event j

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic geometric and handling-constrained routing, without fixing dimension or unloading policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A loading-constrained routing instance augments each transported request \(i\) with a physical item and each vehicle \(k\) with loading space \(S_k\). For every route event \(j\), the carried set \(C_{kj}\) must admit placements \(P_i\subseteq S_k\) such that each item is contained in \(S_k\), interiors of distinct placed items do not overlap, and all prescribed orientation, support, fragility, weight-distribution, stacking, and accessibility rules hold. If rearrangement is forbidden, the placements must evolve between events only by inserting the serviced pickup item or removing the serviced delivery item. Routing feasibility therefore includes both network-route feasibility and loading feasibility at every event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loading-constrained routing requires each route's simultaneously carried items to fit physically and obey orientation, support, stacking, accessibility, and rearrangement rules at every service event.
knowledge_statements.title: Loading-Constrained Routing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is suitable for Loading-Constrained Routing, but the statement combines a broad collection of geometric, support, stacking, accessibility, weight-distribution, and rearrangement rules. Without a cited loading-constrained VRP source and specific locator, this generalized scope and the placement-evolution condition cannot be verified.

children.title: Precedence-Constrained Routing
children.top_down_role: Routing settings requiring specified visit or service orders.

assumptions_latex: The required service events form a finite set \(U\).
A precedence relation \(\prec\) on \(U\) is acyclic.
Each event is assigned to exactly one applicable vehicle route.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A route sequence is precedence-feasible exactly when its ordering is a linear extension of the required precedence relation restricted to that route.

notation.meaning: position of event u on its route

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Route-order precedence, including paired pickup-before-delivery restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be the service events and let \(\prec\) be an acyclic strict precedence relation. A routing solution is precedence-feasible when, for every required pair \(u\prec v\), events \(u\) and \(v\) are assigned compatibly and their route positions satisfy \(\pi(u)<\pi(v)\). In a paired pickup-and-delivery problem, compatibility additionally requires \(p_i\) and \(d_i\) to lie on the same vehicle route, with \(p_i\prec d_i\). Thus each vehicle's service sequence must be a linear extension of the precedence relation induced by the events assigned to that vehicle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precedence-constrained routing requires each vehicle's service sequence to extend the prescribed acyclic event order, including pickup-before-delivery requirements when applicable.
knowledge_statements.title: Precedence-Constrained Routing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A feasibility condition is a reasonable content kind for this leaf. The linear-extension characterization is plausible, but the phrase 'assigned compatibly' leaves cross-route precedence semantics unspecified, and no source is supplied to determine the intended routing model or validate the characterization.

children.title: Loading–Precedence Interactions
children.top_down_role: Cases where physical load access and required visit order constrain each other.

assumptions_latex: Route events obey an acyclic precedence relation \(\prec\).
Loading follows a specified access discipline, such as last-in-first-out.
Items cannot be rearranged except as explicitly allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A precedence-feasible route is jointly feasible only if its induced pickup and delivery order also belongs to the loading discipline's admissible event-order language.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order compatibility under no-rearrangement loading disciplines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Loading rules can impose precedence constraints beyond \(p_i\prec d_i\). For example, under single-door last-in-first-out loading without rearrangement, if two items overlap in carriage and satisfy \(\pi(p_i)<\pi(p_j)<\pi(d_i)\), then accessibility requires \(\pi(d_j)<\pi(d_i)\). Consequently, satisfying the original precedence relation \(\prec\) is necessary but need not be sufficient for joint feasibility: the complete route order must also satisfy every precedence relation induced by the loading discipline and by the sets of items carried simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Loading accessibility can create additional delivery-order restrictions, so a route satisfying its original precedences may still be infeasible under the chosen loading discipline.
knowledge_statements.title: Loading–Precedence Interactions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property fits the interaction leaf, and the stated nested-order implication is plausible for a single-access no-rearrangement LIFO model. A source with a precise loading-access model is required because the implication depends on compartment geometry, access direction, simultaneous carriage, and the exact meaning of rearrangement.

children.title: Loading-Feasibility Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Route plans invalidated by incompatible packing, access, or ordering requirements.

assumptions_latex: Two items \(a\) and \(b\) use a single-access last-in-first-out compartment.
The service order is \(p_a,p_b,d_a,d_b\).
No unloading and reloading at intermediate events is permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route respects pickup-before-delivery precedence and scalar capacity two, but it is loading-infeasible because item \(b\) blocks item \(a\) at \(d_a\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal order-based failure under LIFO loading without rearrangement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider unit items \(a\) and \(b\), a vehicle of scalar capacity two, and the route order
\[
\pi=(p_a,p_b,d_a,d_b).
\]
Both request precedences \(p_a\prec d_a\) and \(p_b\prec d_b\) hold, and the maximum simultaneous scalar load is two. Nevertheless, in a single-access last-in-first-out compartment, item \(b\), loaded after \(a\), must be removed before \(a\). Because the route requires \(d_a\) before \(d_b\), the load cannot be serviced without rearrangement. Thus scalar capacity and pickup-delivery precedence do not imply loading feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order pickup a, pickup b, deliver a, deliver b satisfies ordinary precedence and capacity two but violates no-rearrangement LIFO accessibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Loading-Feasibility Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct content kind for this terminal container, and the event order is a coherent minimal LIFO obstruction under the stated assumptions. No source or locator supports the adopted single-access LIFO model or establishes this example as the intended loading-feasibility boundary.

children.title: Electric Vehicle-Routing Problems
children.top_down_role: Battery-electric fleets, charging constraints, range limits, energy consumption, plus charging-network effects.

assumptions_latex: Vehicle \(k\) has battery capacity \(E_k\) and initial charge \(e_{k0}\).
Traversing arc \((u,v)\) consumes \(c_{uvk}\ge 0\) energy.
Charging at an eligible node adds a bounded amount of energy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An electric route is energy-feasible exactly when its state of charge remains in \([0,E_k]\) after every travel and charging operation.

notation.meaning: state of charge after event j

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Battery-electric VRP with optional intermediate charging decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An electric vehicle-routing problem augments fleet routes with battery states and charging decisions. If vehicle \(k\) traverses arc \((u,v)\) after event \(j\), its charge changes from \(e_{kj}\) to \(e_{kj}-c_{uvk}\); if it then receives charge \(r_{vk}\ge 0\) at an eligible node \(v\), the next state is \(e_{k,j+1}=e_{kj}-c_{uvk}+r_{vk}\). Every state must satisfy \(0\le e_{kj}\le E_k\), and charging amounts or durations must obey station and route-time restrictions. Customer service, vehicle capacity, and route endpoint constraints remain applicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Electric vehicle routing couples customer routes with battery-state transitions and charging decisions, requiring charge to remain within battery limits throughout every route.
knowledge_statements.title: Electric Vehicle-Routing Problems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Electric Vehicle-Routing Problems, and the battery-resource description is plausible. A source is required to fix the state indexing, charging-event convention, consumption model, and scope of station and timing constraints; none is cited.

children.title: Alternative-Fuel Vehicle-Routing Problems
children.top_down_role: Routing for hydrogen, natural-gas, biofuel, hybrid, or other nonconventional fuel fleets.

assumptions_latex: Each vehicle \(k\) has fuel capacity \(F_k\) and initial fuel \(f_{k0}\).
Traversing arc \((u,v)\) consumes \(g_{uvk}\ge 0\) fuel.
Only compatible refueling stations can replenish a vehicle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A route is fuel-feasible exactly when fuel never becomes negative or exceeds capacity and every replenishment respects compatibility and station restrictions.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic nonconventional-fuel VRP with compatible refueling infrastructure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An alternative-fuel vehicle-routing problem augments each route with a fuel resource. After vehicle \(k\) traverses arc \((u,v)\), its fuel becomes \(f_{kj}-g_{uvk}\); a compatible station may then supply \(r_{vk}\ge 0\), giving \(f_{k,j+1}=f_{kj}-g_{uvk}+r_{vk}\). Feasibility requires \(0\le f_{kj}\le F_k\) at every event, permits replenishment only at stations compatible with the vehicle's fuel technology, and enforces any refueling-time, station-capacity, route-duration, customer-service, and payload constraints specified by the instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative-fuel routing tracks fuel consumption and compatible refueling along customer routes while enforcing tank, station, timing, service, and payload restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternative-Fuel Vehicle-Routing Problems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is appropriate for Alternative-Fuel Vehicle-Routing Problems, but no evidence supports this generic resource-transition formulation or its inclusion of station capacity, compatibility, timing, payload, and service constraints. State indexing and replenishment timing also require a sourced convention.

children.title: Mixed-Energy Fleet Routing
children.top_down_role: Fleet regimes combining multiple propulsion or refueling technologies.

assumptions_latex: Each vehicle \(k\) has an energy technology \(\tau_k\) from a finite set \(T\).
Arc consumption and replenishment eligibility may depend on \(\tau_k\).
Customers have declared vehicle-compatibility requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mixed-energy solution is feasible when every assigned route satisfies customer compatibility and the resource-transition system of its vehicle's energy technology.

notation.meaning: energy state of vehicle k after event j

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heterogeneous fleet whose routes obey technology-specific energy and infrastructure rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Mixed-energy fleet routing uses vehicles \(k\in K\) with technologies \(\tau_k\in T\), such as battery-electric, alternative-fuel, or conventional propulsion. Assigning a customer to vehicle \(k\) is allowed only when their compatibility requirements hold. Along each route, the energy state \(e_{kj}\) follows the consumption and replenishment transition prescribed for \(\tau_k\), remains within that vehicle's resource bounds, and uses only compatible infrastructure. A feasible solution jointly chooses customer assignments, visit sequences, and replenishment decisions; its objective may include routing, fleet, energy, emission, or infrastructure-use costs specified by the instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-energy routing jointly assigns customers and routes to vehicles with different propulsion technologies, each governed by its own resource transitions and compatible infrastructure.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Energy Fleet Routing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Mixed-Energy Fleet Routing, and technology-specific resource systems are a plausible organizing principle. No source establishes the proposed technology taxonomy, compatibility semantics, shared energy-state notation across propulsion types, or asserted objective components.

children.title: Multi-Attribute Vehicle-Routing Problems
children.top_down_role: VRP families formed by combining multiple operational attributes or constraints.

assumptions_latex: A base vehicle-routing instance is given on a network \(G=(V,A)\).
A finite attribute set \(H\) specifies additional route or service constraints.
All attribute-specific state transitions and compatibility predicates are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A solution is feasible exactly when it satisfies the base routing constraints and every active attribute predicate jointly on the same assignments, routes, and states.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: VRP family defined by simultaneous enforcement of multiple nonbasic attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A multi-attribute vehicle-routing problem is a base routing problem augmented by a finite set \(H\) of distinct operational or service attributes, such as time windows, heterogeneous vehicles, multiple depots, pickups and deliveries, loading rules, or energy resources. For a candidate solution \(x\), let \(F_0(x)\) denote base-route feasibility and let \(F_h(x)\) denote feasibility for attribute \(h\in H\). The joint feasible set is
\[
\{x:F_0(x)\text{ holds and }F_h(x)\text{ holds for every }h\in H\}.
\]
Attribute constraints are evaluated jointly because they may share assignments, route order, time, load, or resource states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-attribute VRP enforces several operational or service attributes simultaneously, including their interactions through shared routes, assignments, times, loads, and resource states.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Attribute Vehicle-Routing Problems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the appropriate mathematical role for Multi-Attribute Vehicle-Routing Problems, and the joint-predicate expression is internally consistent. An authoritative rich-VRP or multi-attribute VRP source with a specific locator is required to support which features count as distinct attributes and the exact breadth of this family.

children.title: Rich Vehicle-Routing Problems
children.top_down_role: Highly integrated routing settings with extensive operational detail.

knowledge_statements.title: Rich Vehicle-Routing Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rich VRPs by simultaneous, interacting operational attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) contain depot set \(D\) and customer set \(N=V\setminus D\), and let \(K\) be a fleet. A rich vehicle-routing problem is an optimization problem \[\min_{x\in\mathcal X}\; C(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_r(x,a^1,\ldots,a^m)\le 0,\qquad r\in R,\] where \(x\) specifies vehicle routes and service decisions, \(m\ge 2\) operational attributes are modeled simultaneously, and at least one constraint or objective term depends jointly on two attributes. Attributes may describe capacities, time windows, pickups and deliveries, fleet heterogeneity, synchronization, or uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rich VRP jointly models at least two operational attributes, with some feasibility constraint or cost term coupling those attributes.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a finite routing graph with specified depots and customers.
\(K\) and all deterministic attribute data are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a rich-VRP feasible set when at least one modeled relation is nonseparable across operational attributes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but the proposed requirement of at least two attributes with a jointly dependent term is a taxonomy-specific definition unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Attribute-Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural interactions, compatibility boundaries, plus coupling effects among routing attributes.

knowledge_statements.title: Attribute-Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies modeled VRP attributes by mathematical separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For attribute blocks \(a^1,\ldots,a^m\), write the feasible set and objective as \(\mathcal X(a^1,\ldots,a^m)\) and \(C(x;a^1,\ldots,a^m)\). The regime is separable if \[\mathcal X=\bigcap_{j=1}^{m}\mathcal X_j(a^j),\qquad C(x;a^1,\ldots,a^m)=C_0(x)+\sum_{j=1}^{m}C_j(x;a^j).\] It is constraint-coupled if some defining constraint depends on at least two attribute blocks, objective-coupled if a nonadditive objective term depends jointly on them, and decision-coupled if a shared decision variable appears in restrictions induced by distinct blocks. Multiple coupling labels may hold simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attribute regimes are separable when feasibility intersects attribute-wise sets and cost is additive; otherwise coupling may occur through constraints, objectives, or shared decisions.
assumptions_latex: All attribute-specific feasible sets use a common decision space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicates classify an instance as separable, constraint-coupled, objective-coupled, or decision-coupled.

notation.meaning: The data block for attribute j.
Feasibility restrictions induced by attribute j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the separability predicates and coupling labels are bespoke. In particular, shared-variable decision coupling is not shown to be distinct from the displayed separable regime.

children.title: Adaptive-Uncertainty VRP Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Routing-specific model families are retained here; general uncertainty and online-policy theory remains external.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Vehicle Routing: Problems, Methods, and Applications, Second Edition
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Vehicle Routing: Problems, Methods, and Applications, Second Edition

children.title: Stochastic-Demand VRP
children.top_down_role: Routing settings with uncertain customer demand quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Demand VRP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses random customer quantities with nonanticipative routing decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each customer \(i\in N\) have random demand \(Q_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R_+\), and let vehicles have capacity \(B_k\). A stochastic-demand VRP selects a nonanticipative routing policy \(\pi\) whose action at each decision epoch is measurable with respect to the demand information revealed by that epoch. Its canonical risk-neutral form is \[\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{NA}}}\;\mathbb E\!\left[C(\pi,Q)\right],\] subject to scenario-wise route, service, and capacity rules, possibly using prescribed recourse when realized cumulative demand exceeds available capacity. The random primitive distinguishing this class is customer demand rather than customer presence or arc travel time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Customer demands are random, and routes or recourse actions must use only demands revealed so far while minimizing expected routing cost.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) and the fleet are finite.
\(C(\pi,Q)\) is measurable and has a defined expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An admissible solution belongs to \(\Pi_{\mathrm{NA}}\) and satisfies the specified capacity and recourse rules under each relevant realization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the stochastic-demand leaf, but no source supports the selected policy-based, scenario-wise formulation or its relationship to a priori stochastic-demand VRP variants.

children.title: Stochastic-Customer VRP
children.top_down_role: Routing settings with uncertain customer presence, requests, or service incidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Customer VRP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines routing with random customer presence or service requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each potential customer \(i\in N\), let \(Z_i:\Omega\to\{0,1\}\) indicate whether service is required. A stochastic-customer VRP chooses an a priori plan or a nonanticipative policy \(\pi\), then serves exactly the realized active set \(N(\omega)=\{i\in N:Z_i(\omega)=1\}\), subject to the stated fleet and route constraints. A canonical risk-neutral objective is \[\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{NA}}}\;\mathbb E\!\left[C(\pi,Z)\right].\] The defining stochastic primitive is customer activation, presence, or service requirement; demands and travel times may otherwise be deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The set of customers requiring service is random, and feasible routing decisions must serve the realized active customers without anticipating future revelations.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) and the fleet are finite.
\(C(\pi,Z)\) is measurable and integrable for every admissible policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each realization \(\omega\), the executed routes serve precisely the required set \(N(\omega)\) under the model's feasibility rules.

notation.meaning: Indicator that customer i requires service.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but a citation is required to support customer activation as the defining primitive and the combined treatment of a priori plans and adaptive nonanticipative policies.

children.title: Stochastic-Travel-Time VRP
children.top_down_role: Routing settings with uncertain arc, path, or service travel durations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Travel-Time VRP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines routing when arc traversal durations are random.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_{ij}(t,\omega)\ge 0\) be the travel time on arc \((i,j)\in A\) when entered at time \(t\). A stochastic-travel-time VRP selects a nonanticipative routing and scheduling policy \(\pi\). Along an executed route, arrival times obey \[S_{r+1}=S_r+T_{v_rv_{r+1}}(S_r,\omega)+H_{v_r},\] where \(H_{v_r}\) is service duration. The objective minimizes an expectation or specified risk functional of travel, lateness, or completion cost, while feasibility requirements such as time windows are imposed almost surely, by chance constraints, or through penalties as explicitly selected by the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arc travel durations are random; route and schedule decisions use revealed information, and arrival times propagate through realized travel and service times.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) and the fleet are finite.
Travel-time variables and the resulting cost are measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible policy is nonanticipative and its realized arrival times satisfy the displayed recursion and the selected temporal feasibility convention.

notation.meaning: Random time to traverse arc (i,j) after entry at time t.
Arrival time at route position r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the time-dependent recursion or the broad combination of almost-sure, chance-constrained, and penalty-based temporal conventions.

children.title: A Priori Routing Models
children.top_down_role: Models centered on routes committed before uncertain outcomes become known.

knowledge_statements.title: A Priori Routing Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines routes committed before uncertain information is observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi:\Omega\to\Xi\) denote uncertain routing data. An a priori routing model chooses a route plan \(x\in X\) before observing \(\xi\); hence \(x\) is constant with respect to the information generated by \(\xi\). A canonical formulation is \[\min_{x\in X}\;\rho\!\left(C(x,\xi)\right),\] where \(\rho\) is a specified expectation or risk functional. If execution rules skip inactive customers, replenish after excess demand, or otherwise react mechanically, those rules are fixed as part of evaluating \(C(x,\xi)\) and do not permit reoptimization of the committed route order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An a priori model fixes its route plan before uncertainty is observed; only predeclared execution rules may react to realizations.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the set of admissible pre-observation route plans.
\(C(x,\xi)\) lies in the domain of the selected risk functional \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decision \(x\) cannot depend on the realized value of \(\xi\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but the boundary between a fixed route plan, mechanical execution rules, and prohibited reoptimization requires a specific stochastic-routing source.

children.title: Recourse Routing Models
children.top_down_role: Models centered on corrective routing decisions after information is revealed.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Routing Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines routing decisions adapted to successively revealed uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^{T}\) be the information filtration generated by routing observations, and let \(u_t\) be the routing action at epoch \(t\). A recourse routing model optimizes over policies \(\pi=(u_0,\ldots,u_T)\) such that \(u_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable for every \(t\). Its canonical form is \[\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{NA}}}\;\rho\!\left(C(\pi,\xi)\right),\] subject to state-transition, service, fleet, and resource constraints. Thus actions may depend on observed demands, requests, travel times, or vehicle states, but not on information revealed after the action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recourse model allows route actions to adapt to current observations while prohibiting dependence on future information.
assumptions_latex: Decision epochs \(t=0,\ldots,T\) are specified.
Policy costs lie in the domain of \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissibility requires \(u_t\) to be \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable at every decision epoch.

children.title: Commitment–Recourse Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between initial route commitments plus later corrective flexibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Commitment–Recourse Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage representation linking pre-observation commitments and post-observation routing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in X\) be a route commitment selected before uncertainty \(\xi\) is observed, and let \(Y(x,\xi)\) be the feasible recourse decisions compatible with that commitment. The commitment–recourse model is represented by \[\inf_{x\in X}\left\{c(x)+\rho\!\left(Q(x,\xi)\right)\right\},\qquad Q(x,\xi)=\inf_{y\in Y(x,\xi)}q(x,y,\xi).\] Compatibility constraints in \(Y(x,\xi)\) preserve the committed components of \(x\), while allowing only the specified rerouting, replenishment, rejection, reassignment, or scheduling responses. If \(Y(x,\xi)=\varnothing\), the model must assign infeasibility or a declared penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-stage route commitment is evaluated through the optimal permitted response to each realization, with compatibility constraints linking both stages.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is selected before \(\xi\) is observed.
The risk functional \(\rho\) is defined on the recourse-value random variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total value equals commitment cost plus the risk-adjusted optimal compatible recourse value.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the appropriate kind, but the two-stage formulation, compatibility interpretation, and handling of empty recourse sets require a specific two-stage routing or stochastic-programming citation.

children.title: Dynamic-Request VRP
children.top_down_role: Routing with requests revealed, revised, or withdrawn during operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Request VRP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines online routing with requests revealed during operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic-request VRP has requests \(r\in R\) with revelation times \(\tau_r\), locations, service requirements, and possibly deadlines that become known only at \(\tau_r\). At each time \(t\), a routing policy chooses dispatch, insertion, acceptance, or rejection actions using only \[\mathcal I_t=\sigma\!\left(\{r:\tau_r\le t\},\text{observed fleet states through }t\right).\] Previously executed travel is irreversible, and every accepted request must satisfy the declared service constraints. The objective aggregates travel and service cost and any rejection, lateness, or waiting penalties over the operating horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requests arrive during operation; routing actions use only requests and fleet states observed so far, while completed travel cannot be revised.
assumptions_latex: The operating horizon and initial fleet state are specified.
Each revealed request supplies all data needed by the model's service rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every decision at time \(t\) is \(\mathcal I_t\)-measurable and respects irreversible past actions.

notation.meaning: Set of requests realized over the horizon.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but the information structure, irreversibility requirement, and acceptance or rejection conventions lack a supporting dynamic-VRP source.

children.title: Dynamic Vehicle-Availability VRP
children.top_down_role: Routing with vehicles entering, leaving, failing, or changing availability during operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Vehicle-Availability VRP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines routing with fleet availability changing during operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k(t)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether vehicle \(k\in K\) is available for dispatch or continued service at time \(t\). A dynamic vehicle-availability VRP chooses routing and assignment actions adapted to the observed availability history. An action assigning work to vehicle \(k\) at time \(t\) is feasible only if \(A_k(t)=1\) and the vehicle's location, load, and remaining resources permit it. Availability changes may arise from release times, shifts, breakdowns, repairs, or external commitments; the model must specify the transition and treatment of work assigned when availability is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vehicle usability changes over time, so assignments must adapt to observed availability and each vehicle's current operational state.
assumptions_latex: The finite fleet \(K\) has specified initial states.
Availability and vehicle-state histories are observable according to a stated information pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every time \(t\), dispatched vehicles satisfy \(A_k(t)=1\) and all current state-dependent resource restrictions.

notation.meaning: Availability indicator for vehicle k at time t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but the single availability indicator combines dispatch eligibility and continued-service capability across materially different release, shift, breakdown, repair, and commitment models without a source.

children.title: Coupled Request–Fleet Dynamics
children.top_down_role: Settings where evolving requests interact directly with evolving fleet availability.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Request–Fleet Dynamics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes interaction between evolving requests and fleet states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_t\) be the requests known by time \(t\), \(S_t\) the fleet state, and \(u_t\) the routing action. Request and fleet dynamics are coupled when their joint transition satisfies \[(R_{t+1},S_{t+1})=F_t(R_t,S_t,u_t,W_{t+1})\] and cannot be represented simultaneously as \(R_{t+1}=F_t^R(R_t,W_{t+1}^R)\) and \(S_{t+1}=F_t^S(S_t,u_t,W_{t+1}^S)\). Equivalently, some request evolution depends on fleet state or action, or some fleet transition depends on request realization or service. Admissible \(u_t\) must be measurable with respect to the history observed through \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Request and fleet processes are coupled when one process's transition depends on the other process or on shared routing actions.
assumptions_latex: Time is indexed by specified decision epochs.
The joint state and disturbance process are measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coupling holds exactly when no stated componentwise transition factorization describes both dynamics.

notation.meaning: Known request state at epoch t.
Routing or service action at epoch t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the nonfactorization criterion is taxonomy-specific, and the claimed equivalence with cross-process dependence is not reliable without precise disturbance and functional-dependence assumptions.

children.title: Robust Vehicle-Routing Problems
children.top_down_role: Routing under uncertainty sets without a distributional ambiguity layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Vehicle-Routing Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust formulation with deterministic uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be a prescribed uncertainty set for demands, travel times, service times, or other routing data \(\xi\). A static robust vehicle-routing problem is \[\min_{x\in X}\;\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal U} C(x,\xi)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_j(x,\xi)\le 0\ \text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal U\text{ and }j\in J.\] Here \(x\) is selected without knowing \(\xi\). An adjustable robust variant additionally permits designated recourse variables \(y(\xi)\) that obey the declared information structure, while the first-stage route commitments remain common to all realizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust VRP selects routes feasible for every realization in an uncertainty set and typically minimizes their worst-case cost.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the deterministic route-decision domain.
\(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\) is specified independently of the decision unless decision dependence is explicitly modeled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A robust-feasible decision satisfies \(g_j(x,\xi)\le 0\) for all \(j\in J\) and all \(\xi\in\mathcal U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf and the static robust formulation is standard, but no citation supports it here, and the appended adjustable variant requires a source clarifying its information structure and distinction from static robustness.

children.title: Distributionally Robust Vehicle-Routing Problems
children.top_down_role: Routing under ambiguity sets over probability distributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Vehicle-Routing Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage distributionally robust routing with first-stage routes and uncertainty-dependent recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a set of feasible first-stage fleet-routing decisions, \(\xi\in\Xi\) uncertain demands, travel times, or service times, and \(Q(x,\xi)\) the optimal recourse cost after observing \(\xi\). Given an ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) of probability distributions on \(\Xi\), a distributionally robust vehicle-routing problem is
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\left\{c(x)+\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\right\}.
\]
Feasibility may additionally require \(P\)-almost-sure recourse feasibility for every \(P\in\mathcal P\), or a specified worst-case chance constraint. The ambiguity set and information available to recourse decisions are part of the model definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose initial routes to minimize routing cost plus the largest expected recourse cost over an ambiguity set of probability laws.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal P\neq\varnothing\).
\(Q(x,\xi)\) is measurable and has defined expectation for every modeled \(x\) and \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{DRO}}=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[Q(x,\xi)]\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical two-stage distributionally robust optimization specialization to vehicle routing
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this particular two-stage vehicle-routing specialization or its recourse-feasibility variants.

children.title: Robustness-Regime Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Comparative scope, conservatism, tractability, plus failure boundaries across robustness regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness-Regime Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value ordering for nominal stochastic, distributionally robust, and support-robust routing models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a common feasible routing set \(X\), cost \(c(x)\), loss \(Q(x,\xi)\), nominal law \(P_0\), ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\), and uncertainty support \(U\). Define
\[
v_{P_0}=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\mathbb E_{P_0}Q(x,\xi)\},\quad
v_{\mathcal P}=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_PQ(x,\xi)\},
\]
\[
v_U=\inf_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\sup_{\xi\in U}Q(x,\xi)\}.
\]
If \(P_0\in\mathcal P\) and every \(P\in\mathcal P\) is supported on \(U\), then \(v_{P_0}\le v_{\mathcal P}\le v_U\). This comparison requires identical decisions, recourse, and feasibility conventions across regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With nested uncertainty descriptions and identical feasible policies, nominal stochastic cost is no larger than distributionally robust cost, which is no larger than support-robust cost.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\in\mathcal P\).
\(P(U)=1\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P\).
All displayed expectations and infima are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{P_0}\le v_{\mathcal P}\le v_U\).

children.title: Two-Index Vehicle-Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Vehicle-flow formulations indexed primarily by arc endpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Index Vehicle-Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregated arc-flow representation of the capacitated VRP with identical vehicles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V_0,A)\), with depot \(0\), customers \(V\), demands \(d_i>0\), capacity \(Q\), and \(m\) identical vehicles. A two-index vehicle-flow representation uses \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) to indicate that some vehicle traverses arc \((i,j)\). It imposes
\[
\sum_jx_{ij}=\sum_jx_{ji}=1\quad(i\in V),\qquad
\sum_jx_{0j}=\sum_ix_{i0}=m,
\]
and, for every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\),
\[
\sum_{i\in S,\,j\notin S}x_{ij}\ge \left\lceil\frac{\sum_{i\in S}d_i}{Q}\right\rceil.
\]
With admissible arcs and routing costs specified, these constraints represent depot-rooted capacity-feasible routes without naming individual vehicles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary arc variables aggregate identical vehicles; degree, depot-count, and capacity-cut constraints encode a capacitated fleet of depot-rooted routes.
assumptions_latex: \(0<d_i\le Q\) for every \(i\in V\).
Vehicles are identical and each customer is visited exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) represents an aggregated collection of \(m\) capacity-feasible depot routes.

notation.meaning: use of directed arc from node i to node j

children.title: Three-Index Vehicle-Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Vehicle-flow formulations carrying an additional vehicle or route index.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Index Vehicle-Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vehicle-disaggregated arc-flow representation for a capacitated fleet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index vehicles. A three-index formulation uses \(x_{ijk}\in\{0,1\}\) for traversal of \((i,j)\) by vehicle \(k\), and \(y_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\) for assignment of customer \(i\) to \(k\). It imposes
\[
\sum_{k\in K}y_{ik}=1,
\quad \sum_jx_{ijk}=y_{ik},
\quad \sum_jx_{jik}=y_{ik}
\quad(i\in V,k\in K),
\]
\[
\sum_{i\in V}d_i y_{ik}\le Q\quad(k\in K),
\]
together with depot flow and subtour-elimination constraints for each vehicle. Thus every selected arc is assigned to a named vehicle and each vehicle's route and capacity are represented separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arc variables carry a vehicle index, allowing assignment, route continuity, and capacity to be enforced separately for every vehicle.
assumptions_latex: \(0<d_i\le Q\) for every customer \(i\).
Each vehicle begins and ends at depot \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\) represents customer-disjoint, vehicle-specific, capacity-feasible depot routes.

notation.meaning: customer i is assigned to vehicle k

children.title: Vehicle-Index Aggregation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between aggregated vehicle flows plus explicitly indexed vehicle flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Vehicle-Index Aggregation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer correspondence and information loss when indices of identical vehicles are aggregated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For identical vehicles indexed by \(K=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define the aggregation map on a feasible three-index integer solution by
\[
x_{ij}=\sum_{k\in K}x_{ijk}.
\]
Every such indexed solution maps to an aggregated integer arc flow representing the same multiset of unlabeled routes. Conversely, any aggregated integer solution that decomposes into at most \(m\) depot-rooted feasible routes can be labeled with distinct indices in \(K\), producing a compatible three-index solution. Aggregation therefore preserves these decomposable unlabeled integer routes but removes vehicle identity. Formulation-specific linking, symmetry-breaking, and subtour constraints may cause the projected linear-programming relaxations to differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For identical vehicles, labeling or aggregating decomposable integer routes preserves the unlabeled routes, but aggregation removes vehicle identity and need not preserve the formulation's linear relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) indexes vehicles with identical capacities, costs, and admissible-route rules.
The compared formulations use compatible route-feasibility constraints.
The aggregated integer solution decomposes into at most \(m\) depot-rooted feasible routes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\sum_{k\in K}x^k:x^k\text{ form an indexed integer solution}\}\) equals the set of compatible decomposable aggregated integer route flows.

notation.meaning: index set of available identical vehicles

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: route labeling and summation support the qualified integer aggregation correspondence

children.title: Single-Commodity-Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Compact VRP formulations using one auxiliary flow commodity.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Commodity-Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity representation using one aggregate load flow on selected routing arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a directed capacitated VRP, let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) select routing arcs and let \(f_{ij}\ge0\) denote aggregate commodity carried from the depot toward unserved customers. A single-commodity-flow representation imposes
\[
\sum_j f_{ji}-\sum_j f_{ij}=d_i\quad(i\in V),
\qquad 0\le f_{ij}\le Qx_{ij}\quad((i,j)\in A),
\]
together with customer degree and depot fleet constraints on \(x\). Flow conservation forces every positive-demand customer to be connected to the depot, while the arc-linking bounds restrict the aggregate load carried by each selected vehicle arc to capacity \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One continuous flow tracks aggregate delivered load; balance and arc-capacity links enforce depot connectivity and vehicle capacity alongside routing constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(d_i>0\) and \(d_i\le Q\) for every \(i\in V\).
The arc orientation follows movement from the depot toward deliveries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,f)\) jointly encodes routing arcs and a capacity-bounded aggregate delivery flow.

notation.meaning: aggregate undelivered commodity transported on arc (i,j)

children.title: Multicommodity-Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Compact VRP formulations using customer-specific or multiple auxiliary flow commodities.

knowledge_statements.title: Multicommodity-Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Customer-disaggregated delivery flows linked to a common routing vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each customer \(h\in V\), let \(z^h_{ij}\in[0,1]\) be flow of commodity \(h\) on arc \((i,j)\). A multicommodity-flow VRP representation requires one unit to travel from depot \(0\) to \(h\):
\[
\sum_jz^h_{0j}-\sum_jz^h_{j0}=1,
\quad
\sum_jz^h_{ji}-\sum_jz^h_{ij}=\begin{cases}1,&i=h,\\0,&i\in V\setminus\{h\},\end{cases}
\]
and links flows to route selection by
\[
0\le z^h_{ij}\le x_{ij},
\qquad
\sum_{h\in V}d_hz^h_{ij}\le Qx_{ij}.
\]
Customer-degree and depot constraints complete the routing representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separate depot-to-customer flow identifies each customer's delivery path, with shared arc links enforcing route selection and total vehicle capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(0<d_h\le Q\) for every \(h\in V\).
\(x\) satisfies the associated customer-degree and depot constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,z)\) represents selected routing arcs with customer-specific delivery paths and capacity coupling.

notation.meaning: flow for customer commodity h on arc (i,j)

children.title: Commodity-Disaggregation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Formulation size, relaxation strength, plus symmetry effects across commodity granularities.

knowledge_statements.title: Commodity-Disaggregation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapping, size, and relaxation consequences of aggregating customer commodities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a feasible multicommodity vector \(z\), define the aggregate flow
\[
f_{ij}=\sum_{h\in V}d_hz^h_{ij}.
\]
Commodity conservation and the shared capacity constraint imply the single-commodity balance equations and \(0\le f_{ij}\le Qx_{ij}\). Hence every multicommodity relaxation point projects to a single-commodity point. The converse need not hold fractionally because an aggregate flow need not admit customer-specific paths compatible with the same \(x\). Multicommodity formulations retain commodity identity and may strengthen the relaxation, but use \(O(|V||A|)\) flow variables rather than \(O(|A|)\); integer-feasible routes admit both representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated customer flows map to aggregate load flow and can strengthen fractional formulations, at the cost of a customer factor in model size.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations use the same directed graph, routing variables, demands, and capacity.
Flow orientations and balance conventions are compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_{ij}=\sum_h d_hz^h_{ij}\) maps multicommodity feasibility into single-commodity feasibility, but fractional reverse lifting is not guaranteed.
