children.title: Time-Indexed VRP Models
children.top_down_role: Formulations whose principal expanded state dimension is time.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Indexed VRP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete state-expanded routing formulation indexed by service-start time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=\{0,\ldots,H\}\) be a discrete set of service-start times, let \(s_i\) be the service duration at location \(i\), let \(\tau_{ij}\) be the travel time on arc \((i,j)\), and let \([a_i,b_i]\cap T\) be the admissible service-start states at location \(i\). A time-indexed formulation uses a binary variable \(x_{ijtt'}\) for a transition from state \((i,t)\) to state \((j,t')\). Such a variable is created only when
\[
t'\ge t+s_i+\tau_{ij},\qquad t\in[a_i,b_i]\cap T,\qquad t'\in[a_j,b_j]\cap T.
\]
The inequality permits waiting before service at \(j\). Flow conservation is imposed at every internal state \((i,t)\), and one-service constraints require exactly one selected incoming transition over all admissible states of each customer. Depot source and return constraints determine the vehicle paths through the time-expanded network.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routing occurs on a time-expanded network. Each transition respects travel and service duration, may include waiting, and joins admissible service-start states; state flow and visit constraints enforce temporal continuity and one service per customer.
assumptions_latex: \(T=\{0,\ldots,H\}\) is a finite time grid containing all admissible service-start states.
\(s_i\) and \(\tau_{ij}\) are nonnegative and compatible with the chosen time grid.
The horizon \(H\) contains every route represented by the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected state arcs form depot-rooted vehicle paths satisfying the encoded discrete service-time windows and temporal transitions.

notation.meaning: transition from service-start state (i,t) to service-start state (j,t')
service-start time window at location i

children.title: Load-Indexed VRP Models
children.top_down_role: Formulations whose principal expanded state dimension is vehicle load.

knowledge_statements.title: Load-Indexed VRP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-expanded routing formulation indexed by cumulative delivered load.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume integer customer demands and vehicle capacity \(Q\), and let \(L=\{0,1,\ldots,Q\}\). A load-indexed formulation uses a binary variable \(x_{ijq}\) for a transition from location \(i\) with cumulative delivered load \(q\) to customer \(j\), whose successor state is \((j,q+d_j)\). The variable exists only when \(q+d_j\le Q\). Flow conservation matches incoming transitions to outgoing transitions at every customer-load state, and the one-service constraints are
\[
\sum_{i}\sum_{q\in L:\,q+d_j\le Q}x_{ijq}=1\qquad(j\in V).
\]
Together with depot source and sink constraints, these conditions select paths whose cumulative-load coordinate increases by the demand of each served customer and never exceeds \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state-expanded network tracks cumulative delivered load. Each transition adds the next customer's demand, while state conservation, explicit visit constraints, and depot constraints form routes that cannot exceed vehicle capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(d_j\in\{1,\ldots,Q\}\) for every customer \(j\in V\).
Routes begin at depot load state \(0\).
The arc set and depot constraints consistently define permissible starts and returns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected depot path has total served demand at most \(Q\).

notation.meaning: transition from location i at cumulative load q to customer j
demand added when customer j is served

children.title: Resource-Indexed VRP Models
children.top_down_role: Formulations indexed by energy, duration, inventory, or other routing resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Indexed VRP Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General state-expanded formulation for one discretized monotone route resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be a finite resource-state set and let \(g_{ij}:R\to R\cup\{\bot\}\) be the transition induced by traversing \((i,j)\), where \(\bot\) denotes infeasibility. A resource-indexed VRP model creates a state arc
\[
(i,r)\longrightarrow(j,g_{ij}(r))
\]
whenever \(g_{ij}(r)\neq\bot\), and assigns it a binary flow variable. Conservation at internal states, depot source and sink constraints, and one-service constraints for each customer select vehicle paths in the expanded graph. Because infeasible successor states are omitted, every selected path respects the encoded resource bound; time and cumulative load are special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand every location by a finite resource state and allow only feasible state transitions; ordinary path-flow constraints then enforce the resource bound.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite.
Each transition \(g_{ij}\) correctly represents resource consumption and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vehicle paths in the expanded graph project to routes feasible for the encoded resource.

children.title: Multi-Index State Coupling
children.top_down_role: Formulations coupling multiple expanded state dimensions within one representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Index State Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for transitions carrying several resource indices simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a routing state be \((i,r)\), where \(r=(r^1,\ldots,r^p)\) belongs to a finite joint resource-state set \(R\). For each routing arc \((i,j)\), let
\[
G_{ij}(r)=\bigl(g^1_{ij}(r),\ldots,g^p_{ij}(r)\bigr)
\]
when every component transition is feasible, and set \(G_{ij}(r)=\bot\) otherwise. A transition variable \(x_{ijrr'}\) may be positive only if
\[
G_{ij}(r)\neq\bot\qquad\text{and}\qquad r'=G_{ij}(r).
\]
Flow conservation must be imposed at each full joint state \((i,r)\), rather than independently on marginal resource coordinates. Thus every selected path carries one jointly consistent history of all encoded resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each selected transition must update every resource coordinate through one joint successor map, and flow must balance at the complete joint state so that incompatible partial resource histories cannot be combined.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a finite set of joint states \(r=(r^1,\ldots,r^p)\).
\(G_{ij}\) includes every resource interaction relevant to modeled feasibility.
\(\bot\) denotes that at least one required component transition is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every selected path satisfies \(r'=G_{ij}(r)\) on each transition and therefore has a jointly consistent encoded resource history.

notation.meaning: joint successor-state map for routing arc (i,j)
transition variable from joint state (i,r) to joint state (j,r')

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Cartesian-product state flow requires a common successor for every resource coordinate

children.title: Set-Partitioning Models
children.top_down_role: Route-based models organized around exact customer coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Partitioning Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary route formulation requiring each customer to occur on exactly one selected feasible route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be the customer set and \(\mathcal R\) a finite family of feasible vehicle routes. For each \(r\in\mathcal R\), let \(c_r\in\mathbb R\) be its cost and \(a_{ir}=1\) exactly when route \(r\) serves customer \(i\). The route-based set-partitioning model is
\[
\min_{x}\ \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}c_rx_r\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}a_{ir}x_r=1\ \ (i\in V),\quad x_r\in\{0,1\}\ \ (r\in\mathcal R).
\]
Fleet-size, depot, or vehicle-class restrictions may be appended as linear side constraints. Every feasible solution selects routes that serve each customer exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose minimum-cost feasible routes so that every customer belongs to exactly one chosen route, optionally subject to fleet or depot side constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(\mathcal R\) are finite.
Each column represents a route feasible for the underlying routing restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}a_{ir}x_r=1\) for every \(i\in V\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and exact-cover formulation are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the VRP-specific formulation or stated side-constraint extension.

children.title: Set-Covering Models
children.top_down_role: Route-based models permitting coverage beyond exact assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Covering Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary route formulation permitting a customer to occur on more than one selected route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\), \(\mathcal R\), \(c_r\), and \(a_{ir}\) have their route-formulation meanings. The route-based set-covering model is
\[
\min_{x}\ \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}c_rx_r\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}a_{ir}x_r\ge 1\ \ (i\in V),\quad x_r\in\{0,1\}\ \ (r\in\mathcal R).
\]
Linear fleet or vehicle-class constraints may also be imposed. Unlike set partitioning, these constraints permit selected routes to cover a customer repeatedly; consequently, feasibility in this model need not encode an operational assignment unless repeated service can be removed or otherwise interpreted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose minimum-cost feasible routes covering every customer at least once; repeated coverage is allowed and may require later removal or interpretation.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(\mathcal R\) are finite.
Every route column satisfies the underlying single-route feasibility rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}a_{ir}x_r\ge 1\) for every \(i\in V\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-covering representation fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the VRP formulation and operational interpretation of repeated coverage lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Coverage-Regime Transformations
children.top_down_role: Structural passage between exact-coverage plus permissive-coverage route models.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage-Regime Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which repeated route coverage can be removed without worsening cost or violating side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the route family is closed under deleting customer visits: for every \(r\in\mathcal R\) and every retained customer subset, a feasible restricted route \(r'\in\mathcal R\) exists with \(c_{r'}\le c_r\). Suppose also that replacing a route by such a restriction preserves all fleet and vehicle-class side constraints. From any integral set-covering solution, assign each multiply covered customer to one selected route and delete it from the others. The resulting selected restricted routes form a set-partitioning solution of no greater cost. Hence the integral set-covering and set-partitioning optima coincide under these closure and monotonicity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If routes can be shortened by deleting duplicate visits without increasing cost or breaking side constraints, every integral cover converts to an equally good partition.
assumptions_latex: The feasible route family is closed under customer deletion.
Route cost is nonincreasing under deletion.
All master side constraints are preserved by route restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{SP}}=z_{\mathrm{SC}}\) for the integral models.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property belongs in this transformation leaf, but the equality-of-optima claim needs a source and sharper treatment of route identity, duplicate restricted columns, empty routes, and side constraints that count or distinguish vehicles.

knowledge_statements.title: Route-Enumeration Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-column formulation obtained by listing every feasible route before optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite routing instance, let \(\mathcal R\) contain every route satisfying the prescribed depot, capacity, duration, resource, and vehicle-class restrictions. Associate a variable \(x_r\) and cost \(c_r\) with every \(r\in\mathcal R\). A route-enumeration model is the finite mixed-integer program
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}c_rx_r:Ax\mathrel{\diamond}d,\ Hx\mathrel{\triangle}h,\ x\in X\right\},
\]
where \(A\) records customer-route incidence, the first constraints impose partitioning or covering, \(H\) contains master side constraints, and \(X\) specifies route-variable integrality and bounds. Enumeration is exact when \(\mathcal R\) is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate all feasible routes, assign each a variable, and solve the resulting finite set-partitioning or set-covering integer program with side constraints.
assumptions_latex: The instance admits finitely many feasible route columns.
The enumerated family contains every route allowed by the intended formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The route model is exact when \(\mathcal R\) is complete.

notation.meaning: chosen coverage relation, equality or greater-than-or-equal

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits route enumeration, but no source is supplied and the placeholder relation \(\triangle\) is not defined as a precise constraint sense; the domains of \(d\) and \(h\) are also unstated.

children.title: Restricted-Master Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Inputs, outputs, state, plus control boundaries exposed by restricted route masters.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-column linear master solved during route-based column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a current column subset \(\mathcal R'\subseteq\mathcal R\), solve the restricted-master linear program
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{r\in\mathcal R'}c_rx_r:A'x=d,\ H'x=h,\ x\ge0\right\}.
\]
The interface returns a primal solution \(x\), objective value, and dual vectors \((\pi,\mu)\) for the coverage and side constraints. These dual vectors are passed to the pricing interface. If new columns arrive, append their coefficients and costs while preserving the master rows, then reoptimize. If the restricted master is infeasible, an auxiliary feasibility master or artificial columns must first supply a valid dual-pricing state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the current finite master LP, return primal and dual solutions to pricing, append generated routes, and reoptimize until no improving column remains.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R'\) is a finite subset of feasible route columns.
The displayed equalities represent the selected master constraint convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface outputs \((x,\pi,\mu)\) for the current restricted master.

notation.meaning: dual vector for master side rows

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic interface is appropriate for the leaf and distinguishes infeasible restricted masters, but its master, dual-output, and artificial-column conventions require an inspectable column-generation source.

children.title: Pricing Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Inputs, outputs, resource context, plus admissibility boundaries exposed by pricing components.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle mapping master dual variables to a minimum-reduced-cost feasible route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given master dual vectors \((\pi,\mu)\), the pricing interface assigns every feasible route \(r\in\mathcal R\) the reduced cost
\[
\bar c_r=c_r-a_r^{\mathsf T}\pi-h_r^{\mathsf T}\mu,
\]
where \(a_r\) and \(h_r\) are its coverage and side-constraint columns. It solves \(r^*\in\arg\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\bar c_r\) subject to all single-route resource restrictions. If \(\bar c_{r^*}<0\), it returns one or more negative-reduced-cost columns and their coefficients; otherwise it returns a certificate that no improving column exists for the current dual solution. Inequality-row signs must follow the dual convention of the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using master dual prices, find a feasible route of minimum reduced cost; return improving columns or certify that none has negative reduced cost.
assumptions_latex: The master dual solution is feasible under a fixed row-sign convention.
The pricing oracle minimizes reduced cost over the complete feasible route family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_{r^*}\ge0\) certifies absence of an improving route column.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pricing-oracle algorithm fits the leaf and the reduced-cost test is coherent under the stated sign convention, but no source supports the formula and certification claim.

children.title: Master–Pricing Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information exchange, consistency requirements, plus termination boundaries across the two interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Pricing Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-generation loop coordinating restricted-master dual solutions with route pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a restricted route family \(\mathcal R_0\) for which the master LP is feasible, possibly using artificial columns. At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master over \(\mathcal R_t\), obtain dual vectors \((\pi_t,\mu_t)\), and invoke pricing. If pricing returns routes \(S_t\) with negative reduced cost, set \(\mathcal R_{t+1}=\mathcal R_t\cup S_t\) and repeat. If the exact pricing minimum is nonnegative, stop: the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master LP. Integrality, when required, is subsequently enforced by integer optimization or branch-and-price rather than by this LP termination test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate restricted-master optimization and exact pricing; add negative-reduced-cost routes until pricing certifies full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The initial restricted master is feasible.
Every pricing call is exact over the complete route family.
The full master LP has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\bar c_r\ge0\) implies full-master LP optimality.

notation.meaning: restricted route family at iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordination loop and LP-only optimality conclusion fit the leaf, but the exact-pricing termination criterion lacks an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Route Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification of vehicle-route blocks with customer-service constraints retained in a master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let vehicle block \(k\) have finite feasible set \(X_k\), whose elements encode complete feasible routes, and let \(z_k\in\operatorname{conv}(X_k)\). Writing the extreme points as \(v_{kr}\), every block vector has a representation
\[
z_k=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_k}v_{kr}\lambda_{kr},\qquad \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_k}\lambda_{kr}=1,\qquad \lambda_{kr}\ge0.
\]
Substitution into the linking customer-service constraints produces a route-column master LP. The reduced-cost minimization for block \(k\) is a linear optimization problem over \(X_k\), hence a resource-constrained route-pricing problem. Integer restrictions on \(\lambda_{kr}\) recover route selection when required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express each vehicle block as a convex combination of feasible routes, retain customer coupling in the master, and generate route columns by block pricing.
assumptions_latex: Each vehicle block has a finite feasible route set \(X_k\).
Coupling constraints and costs are linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k\in\operatorname{conv}(X_k)\) is represented by route weights \(\lambda_{kr}\).

notation.meaning: feasible route set for vehicle block k
route extreme point r of block k

children.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposed VRP structures coordinated through Lagrangian multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable Lagrangian dual obtained by dualizing linear coupling equalities between otherwise independent blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the minimization problem
\[
z^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{k=1}^m(c^k)^{\mathsf T}x^k:x^k\in X_k\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,m,\ \sum_{k=1}^m A_kx^k=b\right\}.
\]
For a multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\), its Lagrangian value is
\[
L(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{k=1}^m\inf_{x^k\in X_k}\bigl((c^k)^{\mathsf T}+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_k\bigr)x^k.
\]
Evaluation therefore separates into independent block problems. The Lagrangian dual value is \(z_L=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p}L(\lambda)\), and \(L(\lambda)\le z^*\) whenever the block infima are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualize the linear coupling equalities so that evaluation separates into independent block problems; maximizing the resulting lower bound gives the Lagrangian dual value.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_k\) is nonempty.
The original problem is a minimization problem with independent block domains coupled only by the displayed equalities.
Every block infimum is finite at each multiplier being evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(\lambda)\le z^*\) for every evaluated \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(z_L=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p}L(\lambda)\le z^*\).

notation.meaning: free multiplier vector for the coupling equalities
optimal value of the original coupled minimization problem

children.title: Lagrangian Relaxation
children.top_down_role: VRP relaxations formed by moving selected coupling requirements into the objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bounding relaxation formed by pricing selected routing constraints into the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) contain the constraints retained explicitly in a minimization problem, and let the relaxed constraints be \(g(x)\le0\). For any multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\), define
\[
L(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)\bigr).
\]
For every feasible \(x\), the added term is nonpositive, so \(L(\lambda)\le f(x)\); consequently \(L(\lambda)\le z^*\). The best Lagrangian bound is the dual value \(z_L=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}L(\lambda)\). Equality with \(z^*\) is not guaranteed for discrete routing problems, and the gap depends on the chosen relaxed constraints and formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move selected inequalities into a minimization objective using nonnegative multipliers; each relaxed optimum is a lower bound, maximized by the Lagrangian dual.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem minimizes \(f(x)\) over \(x\in X\) subject to \(g(x)\le0\).
The relaxed infimum is finite for the multiplier considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(\lambda)\le z^*\) for \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(z_L=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}L(\lambda)\le z^*\).

children.title: Multiplier-Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coupling choices, separability patterns, plus bound-quality tradeoffs across Lagrangian structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Coupling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier domains determined by whether relaxed coupling rows are equalities or one-sided inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, each relaxed coupling row determines its admissible multiplier regime. A row \(g_j(x)=0\) has a free multiplier \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\); a row \(g_j(x)\le0\) has \(\lambda_j\ge0\); and a row \(g_j(x)\ge0\) has \(\lambda_j\le0\). If multiple routing blocks share one coupling row, the same multiplier component must price that row in every affected block. Assigning independent multipliers to duplicated copies instead corresponds to a different relaxation unless explicit agreement conditions are retained. These sign and sharing rules are precisely those ensuring the Lagrangian value remains a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality multipliers are free, inequality multipliers have direction-dependent signs, and a shared coupling row must use the same price across all affected blocks.
assumptions_latex: The primal objective is minimized.
Relaxed rows use the displayed zero-right-hand-side conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\), \(\lambda_j\ge0\), or \(\lambda_j\le0\) according to the coupling-row sense.

children.title: Classical Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: VRP decompositions using mathematical-programming subproblem information.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Benders Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point and extreme-ray cuts for a continuous linear subproblem parameterized by master decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y:x\in X,\ Ay\ge b-Bx,\ y\ge0\}\), where \(x\) is the master decision. For fixed \(x\), the subproblem dual is
\[
\max_{u\ge0}\ (b-Bx)^{\mathsf T}u\quad\text{subject to}\quad A^{\mathsf T}u\le d.
\]
Initialize a master in \((x,\theta)\). An optimal dual extreme point \(u\) yields the optimality cut \(\theta\ge(b-Bx)^{\mathsf T}u\); an improving extreme ray \(v\) yields the feasibility cut \((b-Bx)^{\mathsf T}v\le0\). Repeatedly solve the master and subproblem, append violated cuts, and stop when no cut is violated; then the master value equals the original optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate a master problem with a parameterized LP subproblem, adding dual extreme-point optimality cuts or extreme-ray feasibility cuts until none is violated.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the admissible master domain.
The subproblem is a linear program and satisfies the applicable LP duality alternatives.
The original problem has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of a violated Benders cut certifies optimality of the current master solution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm belongs in the classical Benders leaf and its dual signs are plausible, but no source supports the extreme-point, extreme-ray, and termination claims. The master objective and the precise recession-ray conditions also need source-backed specification.

children.title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: VRP decompositions using inference from combinatorial or scheduling subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Benders Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic logic-based Benders scheme for discrete routing master decisions and an exactly solved operational subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given master variables \(x\in X\), master cost \(c(x)\), and a subproblem value \(Q(x)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), initialize a relaxation containing \(x\in X\), \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}\), and valid lower bounds on \(Q\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min\{c(x)+\theta:(x,\theta)\in M_k\}\), obtaining \((x^k,\theta^k)\). Solve the routing or scheduling subproblem at \(x^k\). If it is infeasible, add a logically valid cut excluding \(x^k\) and every assignment sharing its infeasibility explanation. If it is feasible with value \(Q(x^k)\), add a valid inference cut implying \(\theta\ge Q(x^k)\) at \(x^k\), preferably on a larger explained set. Stop when the master lower bound equals the best feasible objective within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteratively solve a discrete master and an exact routing subproblem, adding explanation-derived feasibility or value cuts until the lower and upper bounds agree.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite or the master admits finite exact optimization.
Every generated inference cut is valid for all \(x\in X\).
The subproblem is solved exactly whenever it is queried.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon finite termination with zero tolerance, the incumbent minimizes \(c(x)+Q(x)\) over \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: optimal subproblem value, with positive infinity denoting infeasibility
master lower approximation of the subproblem value

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard logic-based Benders master–subproblem cut loop

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf and the scheme is plausible, but no inspectable source supports the stated cut requirements or finite optimality conclusion.

children.title: Hybrid Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: VRP decompositions combining classical dual information with logic-based inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Benders Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders framework combining algebraic dual cuts with combinatorial or logic-derived cuts for routing models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a mixed routing formulation into master decisions \(x\in X\) and subproblem decisions. Initialize a master relaxation with \(\theta\) and any valid cuts. At iteration \(k\), solve the master for \((x^k,\theta^k)\), then solve the subproblem. Generate a set \(C_k^{\mathrm{alg}}\) of valid classical Benders cuts from linear-program dual information and a set \(C_k^{\mathrm{logic}}\) of valid combinatorial cuts from infeasibility explanations, route structure, or exact subproblem reasoning. Add any nonempty subset of violated cuts from \(C_k^{\mathrm{alg}}\cup C_k^{\mathrm{logic}}\). Maintain an incumbent from feasible combined solutions and stop when its objective differs from the master lower bound by at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid scheme strengthens a Benders master with both dual-derived linear cuts and problem-specific logical cuts, terminating when its certified gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: All algebraic and logical cuts added to the master are globally valid.
Each queried subproblem is solved sufficiently accurately to certify its cuts and bounds.
\(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the incumbent has objective at most \(\varepsilon\) above the valid master lower bound; for \(\varepsilon=0\), it is optimal.

notation.meaning: classical dual-based cuts generated at iteration k
logic-based or combinatorial cuts generated at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid-cut hybridization of classical and logic-based Benders methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but no source supports this particular hybrid scheme. Valid cuts alone do not establish that the stated stopping condition will be reached.

knowledge_statements.title: Shortest Paths with Resource Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive multi-resource shortest-path formulation used as a column-generation pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), arc costs \(c_a\in\mathbb{R}\), and nonnegative resource consumptions \(r_a\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\). Given resource bounds \(b\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\), a resource-feasible path is an \(s\)-to-\(t\) directed path \(P\) satisfying \(\sum_{a\in P}r_a\le b\) componentwise. The shortest path problem with resource constraints is
\[\min\left\{\sum_{a\in P}c_a: P\text{ is an }s\text{-}t\text{ directed path},\ \sum_{a\in P}r_a\le b\right\}.\]
In pricing, \(c_a\) may be a reduced arc cost, so a negative optimum identifies an improving column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a minimum-cost source-to-sink path whose accumulated consumption of every resource stays within its bound; negative reduced cost yields a pricing column.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is finite.
Resource consumptions are additive and componentwise nonnegative.
Path feasibility is determined by the stated resource bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal value is the least cost among all resource-feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) paths, or \(+\infty\) if none exists.

notation.meaning: vector of resources consumed by arc a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard additive resource-constrained shortest-path formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent, but the available locators cover ordinary shortest paths rather than resource-constrained shortest paths or their pricing interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Resource-Constrained Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary resource-constrained shortest-path pricing for route-based vehicle-routing formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) contain depot vertices \(s,t\) and customer set \(N=V\setminus\{s,t\}\). For reduced arc costs \(\bar c_a\), resource consumptions \(r_a\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\), and bounds \(b\), elementary resource-constrained pricing is
\[\min\left\{\sum_{a\in P}\bar c_a: P\text{ is an }s\text{-}t\text{ path},\ \sum_{a\in P}r_a\le b,\ |P\cap\delta^-(i)|\le1\ \text{for every }i\in N\right\}.\]
The last inequalities impose elementarity: no customer is visited more than once. A feasible path with negative objective represents an improving elementary route column; absence of one certifies pricing optimality for the current restricted master dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing minimizes reduced cost over resource-feasible depot-to-depot paths that visit each customer at most once; a negative optimum supplies an improving route.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is finite and distinguishes depot endpoints from customers.
Resources are additive and bounded componentwise.
Reduced arc costs correspond to a fixed restricted-master dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative optimum yields an elementary feasible route of negative reduced cost; a nonnegative optimum proves that no such route exists.

notation.meaning: reduced cost assigned to arc a

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard elementary resource-constrained shortest-path pricing formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and correctly expresses elementarity through customer-entry counts on a path, but the specialized formulation and pricing certificate have no supporting locator.

children.title: ng-Route Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Pricing relaxations organized around restricted neighborhood memory.

knowledge_statements.title: ng-Route Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood-memory relaxation of elementarity for resource-constrained vehicle-routing pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each customer \(i\in N\), choose a neighborhood \(N_i\subseteq N\) containing \(i\). Along a walk, maintain a memory set \(M\subseteq N\). After extending from the current customer \(i\) to customer \(j\), update
\[M'=(M\cap N_j)\cup\{j\}.\]
The extension is permitted only if \(j\notin M\). An ng-route is a resource-feasible depot-to-depot walk admitted by these memory updates. Its pricing relaxation minimizes reduced cost over all such walks. Every elementary route is an ng-route. If neighborhoods are enlarged componentwise, the admitted route set can only shrink; when \(N_i=N\) for every \(i\), the ng-route set equals the elementary route set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ng-route remembers only locally relevant visited customers, forbidding remembered revisits while allowing some forgotten ones; larger neighborhoods tighten the relaxation toward elementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a finite customer set.
Each neighborhood satisfies \(i\in N_i\subseteq N\).
All walks must also satisfy the underlying pricing resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For neighborhood systems \(N_i\subseteq N_i'\), the feasible sets satisfy \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{elem}}\subseteq\mathcal R_{ng}(N')\subseteq\mathcal R_{ng}(N)\).

notation.meaning: remembered neighborhood associated with customer i
customer-memory set carried by a partial route
ng-route set induced by the neighborhood system

children.title: State-Space Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Pricing relaxations formed by aggregating, omitting, or coarsening state information.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing relaxation obtained by projecting or aggregating exact dynamic-programming states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an exact pricing dynamic program have state space \(S\), transition relation \(T\subseteq S\times S\), and terminal-path set \(\mathcal P(S,T)\). A state-space relaxation is specified by a surjection \(\pi:S\to\widehat S\) and relaxed transitions \(\widehat T\) satisfying
\[(u,v)\in T\Longrightarrow(\pi(u),\pi(v))\in\widehat T.\]
Costs and indispensable resource feasibility information are retained, while selected history components are aggregated or discarded. Consequently, every exact feasible route projects to a relaxed feasible path, so \(\mathcal P(S,T)\) maps into \(\mathcal P(\widehat S,\widehat T)\). For minimization pricing, the relaxed optimum is therefore a lower bound on the exact pricing optimum. Refining \(\pi\) by splitting aggregated states tightens this bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate exact pricing states and preserve all exact transitions. The resulting dynamic program admits a superset of routes and gives a lower bound that tightens under refinement.
assumptions_latex: The exact pricing problem has a finite or finitely representable state-transition model.
Projected transitions preserve the costs of represented exact transitions.
Relaxed states retain all resources declared indispensable for feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimization values satisfy \(z(\widehat S,\widehat T)\le z(S,T)\), and any valid state refinement cannot decrease the relaxed value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dynamic-programming state aggregation yields a relaxation by transition preservation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but transition preservation alone does not fully specify cost handling or guarantee monotonicity under every purported refinement. A source and a precise refinement relation are needed.

children.title: Relaxation-Refinement Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relationships among relaxed state spaces, refinement strength, plus pricing effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Refinement Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive exact-pricing regime that successively removes routes admitted only by a pricing relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose nested pricing-feasible sets \(\mathcal R_0\supseteq\mathcal R_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\mathcal R_*\), where \(\mathcal R_*\) is the exact elementary route set. At stage \(k\), solve reduced-cost pricing over \(\mathcal R_k\). If its optimum is nonnegative, stop: no negative-cost route exists in \(\mathcal R_*\). If a negative-cost optimizer belongs to \(\mathcal R_*\), return it as an improving column. Otherwise identify a violated exactness condition, construct \(\mathcal R_{k+1}\) that excludes that optimizer while retaining \(\mathcal R_*\), and repeat. Refinement may enlarge neighborhoods, restore state components, or forbid a demonstrated repetition pattern. If only finitely many relaxations are available and each unsuccessful refinement is strict, the regime terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve relaxed pricing, accept exact negative routes, and refine away inexact negative routes while preserving all elementary routes; nonnegative relaxed pricing certifies exact pricing.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R_*\subseteq\mathcal R_k\) at every stage.
Each pricing stage is solved exactly.
Every rejected negative route triggers a strict refinement when exact pricing has not yet been reached.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an exact negative-reduced-cost route or certifies that none exists; it terminates finitely under the stated finiteness condition.

notation.meaning: route set admitted at refinement stage k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic nested-relaxation refinement scheme with exact-set preservation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits and the nested-set logic is plausible, but the adaptive regime and its finite-termination claim lack an inspectable specialized source.

children.title: Pricing Label Families
children.top_down_role: Alternative label representations used in resource-constrained route pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Label Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State records representing equivalence classes of partial paths in resource-constrained pricing dynamic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a directed pricing graph, a label at vertex \(v\) is a tuple \(L=(v,\bar c,q,H)\) representing partial paths from the source to \(v\) with reduced cost \(\bar c\), resource state \(q\in Q_v\), and optional history state \(H\). A pricing label family is a collection \(\mathcal L_v\) for each \(v\), together with an interpretation map assigning each label the partial paths it represents. Labels may be forward or backward, exact or relaxed, and history-free or history-augmented. A family is exact when the union of terminal-label interpretations equals precisely the feasible pricing routes and every terminal label carries the corresponding route cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricing label stores endpoint, reduced cost, resources, and optional visit history for represented partial paths; an exact family represents exactly all feasible routes.
assumptions_latex: Each partial path has a well-defined endpoint, accumulated cost, and resource state.
History state records every path feature required by the chosen exactness level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact terminal labels provide a cost-preserving representation of the feasible pricing-route set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional labeling representation for resource-constrained shortest paths

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but the proposed generalized label-family formalization and exactness criterion have no supporting source locator.

children.title: Pricing Dominance Families
children.top_down_role: Dominance regimes for comparing labels under different resource structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Dominance Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe label-elimination predicates for resource-constrained shortest-path pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For labels \(L_1,L_2\) ending at the same vertex, define semantic dominance by
\[L_1\preceq L_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{every feasible completion of }L_2\text{ has a feasible completion of }L_1\text{ with no larger total reduced cost}.\]
A pricing dominance family is any collection of efficiently testable predicates implying this relation. Under additive nonnegative resources and identical admissible-history sets, a standard sufficient predicate is \(\bar c_1\le\bar c_2\) and \(q_1\le q_2\) componentwise. If at least one inequality is strict, \(L_2\) may be discarded without removing every optimal completion. For history-dependent pricing, the predicate must additionally ensure that every continuation allowed after \(L_2\) is allowed after \(L_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One label safely dominates another when it can reproduce every feasible continuation at no greater total reduced cost; dominated labels may be deleted.
assumptions_latex: Compared labels end at the same graph vertex.
Resource extension is monotone under the componentwise resource order.
Any history comparison preserves inclusion of admissible continuation sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting a dominated label preserves the optimal pricing value and at least one optimal terminal route.

notation.meaning: accumulated reduced cost of label i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: continuation-based dominance and componentwise sufficient test are standard in labeling algorithms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits. The continuation-based definition is plausible, but the sufficient componentwise test and preservation claim depend on extension and history assumptions that require authoritative support.

children.title: Resource-Extension Families
children.top_down_role: Resource-extension structures for propagating pricing-state information.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Extension Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc-indexed maps that propagate resource states and determine extension feasibility in pricing labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_i\) be the resource-state domain at vertex \(i\). For every arc \(a=(i,j)\), a resource-extension function is a partial map \(F_a:Q_i\rightharpoonup Q_j\). Extending a label with state \(q\) along \(a\) is feasible exactly when \(F_a(q)\) is defined, and the successor state is \(q'=F_a(q)\). A resource-extension family is \(\{F_a:a\in A\}\). It is path-consistent when, for every path \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\), the composition \(F_P=F_{a_k}\circ\cdots\circ F_{a_1}\) is defined exactly for resource-feasible traversals and returns their resource state. Additive resources use \(F_a(q)=q+r_a\) whenever \(q+r_a\le b\); time-window extensions may additionally apply waiting by a maximum operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each arc has a partial state-update map. A label extension is feasible when that map is defined, and compositions reproduce resources along complete paths.
assumptions_latex: Every vertex \(i\) has a specified resource domain \(Q_i\).
Each arc extension uses only the current state and arc data.
Undefined extension denotes resource infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A path is resource-feasible precisely when its composed resource-extension map is defined at the initial state.

notation.meaning: partial resource-extension map for arc a
composition of extension maps along path P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: resource-extension functions are the standard algebraic basis of constrained-path labeling

children.title: Label–Resource Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility boundaries linking label state, dominance strength, plus resource propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Label–Resource Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency conditions linking label states, resource-extension maps, feasibility, cost, and history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A label family \(\mathcal L\) is compatible with resource-extension maps \(\{F_a\}_{a\in A}\) when the following holds. If \(L=(i,\bar c,q,H)\) represents a partial path \(P\) and \(a=(i,j)\), then an extended label exists exactly when \(F_a(q)\) is defined and the history rule permits \(j\). Every such successor \(L'=(j,\bar c+\bar c_a,F_a(q),H')\) represents precisely the permitted paths \(P+a\), with \(H'\) obtained by the declared history update. Conversely, every feasible one-arc extension of every represented path is represented by some such successor. Thus label propagation is both sound and complete relative to the selected resource and history model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Labels and resource maps are compatible when propagation creates exactly the permitted path extensions with correct endpoint, cost, resources, and history.
assumptions_latex: Labels have endpoint, reduced-cost, resource, and history components.
Arc costs and resource-extension maps are fixed.
A declared history-update rule determines permitted visits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatible propagation is sound and complete: terminal labels represent exactly the routes feasible under the selected resource-history model.

children.title: Bidirectional Pricing Labeling
children.top_down_role: Pricing methods based on forward plus backward label searches.

knowledge_statements.title: Bidirectional Pricing Labeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Meet-in-the-middle labeling algorithm for resource-constrained route pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct forward labels from source \(s\) and backward labels from sink \(t\) using direction-appropriate resource-extension maps. Extend each label only while it satisfies its directional feasibility rules and a prescribed halfway stopping rule. Apply valid dominance within each direction. For every forward label \(L^f\) at vertex \(i\) and backward label \(L^b\) at vertex \(j\), test each admissible joining arc \((i,j)\). Join only if the combined resources satisfy all route bounds, the histories are mutually compatible, and the concatenation is elementary or satisfies the chosen relaxation. Compute the joined reduced cost without double counting. Return the least-cost feasible join; if no join has negative reduced cost, report that no improving route was generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grow labels from both depots, stop near a meeting boundary, and join compatible forward and backward states to find the least-cost feasible route.
assumptions_latex: Directional extension and dominance rules are valid.
Every feasible route admits at least one forward–backward split examined by the join step.
The join test exactly enforces combined resources and history compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum accepted join has the exact pricing optimum; a nonnegative minimum certifies absence of a negative-reduced-cost route.

notation.meaning: forward pricing label grown from the source
backward pricing label grown from the sink
arc used to join forward and backward partial paths

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard bidirectional meet-in-the-middle labeling architecture

children.title: Pricing Completion Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds used to assess the best attainable completion of partial pricing paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Completion Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound certificate for completing a forward pricing label by a compatible backward label.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a forward label \(F\) end at vertex \(v\), have reduced cost \(\bar c(F)\), and admit compatible backward labels \(\mathcal B(F)\). If \(L(F)\) satisfies \[L(F)\leq \min_{B\in\mathcal B(F)}\bar c(B),\] with the minimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(\mathcal B(F)=\varnothing\), then every complete route formed from \(F\) has reduced cost at least \(\bar c(F)+L(F)\). Consequently, when pricing seeks a route of negative reduced cost, \(F\) may be discarded if \(\mathcal B(F)=\varnothing\) or \(\bar c(F)+L(F)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward label is safely pruned when no compatible suffix exists or a certified suffix-cost lower bound makes every completion nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \(L(F)\) is a valid lower bound over all compatible backward completions.
Reduced costs of joined forward and backward portions are additive under the chosen join convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c(F)+L(F)\geq0\) certifies that \(F\) cannot generate a negative-reduced-cost route.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound on compatible suffix reduced cost.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: branch-and-bound lower-bound pruning for bidirectional resource-constrained shortest-path pricing

children.title: Join-Regime Compatibility
children.top_down_role: State compatibility, resource compatibility, plus bounding requirements at bidirectional joins.

knowledge_statements.title: Join-Regime Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for joining elementary forward and backward pricing labels at a common vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let forward label \(F\) and backward label \(B\) meet at \(v\). They are join-compatible precisely when \[V(F)\cap V(B)=\{v\},\qquad r(F)\oplus_v r(B)\in\mathcal R,\qquad (F,B)\in\mathcal J,\] where \(\mathcal R\) is the feasible set for accumulated capacity, time, and other resources, \(\oplus_v\) applies the prescribed correction for the shared vertex, and \(\mathcal J\) contains any direction-, depot-, arc-, or branching-specific join restrictions. Under these conditions, concatenating \(F\) and the reverse-oriented suffix represented by \(B\) produces an elementary resource-feasible route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two labels may be joined exactly when they overlap only at the join vertex, satisfy combined resource limits, and obey regime-specific restrictions.
assumptions_latex: Both labels use the same resource-extension convention.
The backward label represents its suffix in the orientation prescribed by the pricing algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicate is sufficient for the concatenated label pair to represent a feasible elementary route.

notation.meaning: Vertices visited by the two partial routes.
Additional restrictions of the selected join regime.

children.title: Capacity Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Capacity-derived VRP cuts without rounded demand-to-vehicle strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unrounded cut-capacity inequality for an undirected capacitated vehicle-routing formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(\{0\}\cup V,E)\) be an undirected CVRP graph. For each customer \(i\in V\), let \(d_i\geq0\) be its demand, let \(Q>0\) be the vehicle capacity, and let \(x_e\) denote the number of traversals of edge \(e\in E\) in a feasible depot-to-depot route collection. For every nonempty set \(S\subseteq V\), define \(d(S)=\sum_{i\in S}d_i\) and \(x(\delta(S))=\sum_{e\in\delta(S)}x_e\). Every feasible route-incidence vector satisfies \[x(\delta(S))\geq\frac{2d(S)}{Q}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nonempty customer set, the number of boundary-edge traversals is at least twice the set's total demand divided by vehicle capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(\{0\}\cup V,E)\) is an undirected CVRP graph.
Each customer is served exactly once without split deliveries.
Every route starts and ends at depot \(0\) and carries at most \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(\delta(S))\geq 2d(S)/Q\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\).

notation.meaning: Edges having exactly one endpoint in S.
Total traversal count of edges across the cut.
Total demand of customers in S.

children.title: Rounded-Capacity Inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Rounded-Capacity Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer-rounded capacity inequality for an undirected capacitated vehicle-routing formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(\{0\}\cup V,E)\) be an undirected CVRP graph. For each customer \(i\in V\), let \(d_i\geq0\) be its demand, let \(Q>0\) be the vehicle capacity, and let \(x_e\) denote the number of traversals of edge \(e\in E\) in a feasible depot-to-depot route collection. For every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\), define \(d(S)=\sum_{i\in S}d_i\), \(r(S)=\lceil d(S)/Q\rceil\), and \(x(\delta(S))=\sum_{e\in\delta(S)}x_e\). Every feasible integer route-incidence vector satisfies \[x(\delta(S))\geq2r(S)=2\left\lceil\frac{d(S)}{Q}\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nonempty customer set, the number of boundary-edge traversals is at least twice the minimum integer number of vehicle loads required by its total demand.
assumptions_latex: Customers have nonnegative demands and are served exactly once without split deliveries.
Every route starts and ends at depot \(0\).
All vehicles have capacity \(Q>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(\delta(S))\geq2\lceil d(S)/Q\rceil\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\).

notation.meaning: Minimum integer number of vehicle loads required by S.
Total demand of customers in S.
Edges having exactly one endpoint in S.

children.title: Capacity-Cut Strengthening Regimes
children.top_down_role: Relationships among basic capacity cuts, rounded variants, plus lifting regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Cut Strengthening Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance relation between unrounded and rounded CVRP capacity cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty \(S\subseteq V\), the rounded-capacity right-hand side dominates the unrounded one because \[2\left\lceil\frac{d(S)}{Q}\right\rceil\geq\frac{2d(S)}{Q}.\] Hence the rounded inequality implies the unrounded capacity inequality on the same cut. The strengthening is strict exactly when \(d(S)/Q\notin\mathbb Z\). If \(d(S)/Q\in\mathbb Z\), both regimes give the same right-hand side. Thus rounding can remove fractional solutions while leaving the feasible integer route set unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounded capacity cuts dominate unrounded cuts, strictly so unless the set demand is an exact multiple of vehicle capacity.
assumptions_latex: Both inequalities use the same undirected cut expression \(x(\delta(S))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rounded regime dominates the unrounded regime, with equality exactly when \(d(S)/Q\in\mathbb Z\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: immediate ceiling-based dominance of standard CVRP capacity cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Multistar Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation boundary preventing a unique multistar formula from being inferred from the family name alone.

If any of these data are omitted, two inequalities can share the multistar support pattern while having different coefficients or right-hand sides. Consequently, no expression \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\) can be certified as the canonical multistar inequality solely from the family name; validity must be attached to a declared CVRP formulation and multistar construction.

children.title: Comb Inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Comb Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical undirected comb inequality for a connected degree-two tour incidence vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a handle and let \(T_1,\ldots,T_t\) be pairwise disjoint teeth, where \(t\geq3\) is odd and each tooth satisfies \(T_i\cap H\neq\varnothing\) and \(T_i\setminus H\neq\varnothing\). For every incidence vector \(x\) of a connected undirected spanning tour, \[x(\delta(H))+\sum_{i=1}^{t}x(\delta(T_i))\geq 3t+1.\] The statement applies directly only to formulations whose projected integer solutions satisfy the connected degree-two tour structure; a multi-route VRP formulation requires a separately verified adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An odd collection of disjoint teeth crossing a handle forces at least 3t+1 total handle-and-tooth boundary edges in a tour.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is the incidence vector of a connected undirected spanning tour.
The teeth are pairwise disjoint and cross the handle boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(\delta(H))+\sum_{i=1}^{t}x(\delta(T_i))\geq3t+1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Frame Inequalities

In particular, transferring a frame inequality between a tour polytope and a capacitated multi-route formulation can fail because depot multiplicity and route-capacity terms change both validity conditions and coefficients. Therefore a proposed inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\) is admissible under this title only after its complete frame incidence pattern and the integer solution set over which it is valid are declared.

children.title: Structured-Cut Relationships

knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Cut Relationships
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal dominance and specialization conditions for comparing structured VRP cut families over a common relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq P\subseteq\mathbb R^E\), where \(X\) is the target integer feasible set and \(P\) is a common base relaxation. Let \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}x\geq d\) be inequalities valid for \(X\). The first dominates the second relative to \(P\) precisely when \[P\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^E:a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\}\subseteq P\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^E:c^{\mathsf T}x\geq d\}.\] A structured family \(\mathcal F_1\) subsumes \(\mathcal F_2\) by parameter specialization when every member of \(\mathcal F_2\) is obtained from a member of \(\mathcal F_1\) through an explicitly declared specialization of its parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to one base relaxation, one valid cut dominates another when imposing it leaves a subset of the points left by the other; family subsumption by specialization requires an explicit parameter mapping.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq P\subseteq\mathbb R^E\).
All compared inequalities use the same variable space and are valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dominance relative to \(P\) is characterized by the displayed containment, while subsumption by specialization requires an explicit parameter specialization.

children.title: Path Inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Path Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forbidden-path inequality for a resource-infeasible directed path in an arc formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) be a directed path whose simultaneous use by one vehicle is infeasible under the model's capacity, time, pairing, or other route resources. For binary same-route arc variables \(x_a\), every feasible routing solution satisfies \[\sum_{a\in P}x_a\leq k-1.\] Thus at least one arc of every certified infeasible path must be absent. The inequality is valid only when the variables identify arc uses on a common route; aggregate arc variables require a lifting or vehicle-indexed interpretation that preserves this implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a complete directed path cannot occur on one feasible route, at least one of its arcs must be excluded.
assumptions_latex: All arcs of \(P\) would belong to the same vehicle route if selected.
The full path \(P\) has been certified resource-infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{a\in P}x_a\leq |P|-1\).

children.title: Precedence Inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forbidden-path form of a pickup-before-delivery precedence inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose request \(r\) has pickup vertex \(p_r\) and delivery vertex \(d_r\), which must occur on the same route with \(p_r\) preceding \(d_r\). Let \(P\) be any directed same-route path that visits \(d_r\) before \(p_r\). Then \(P\) is precedence-infeasible, and binary arc variables satisfy \[\sum_{a\in P}x_a\leq |P|-1.\] More generally, the same inequality applies to any path whose vertex order violates a declared acyclic precedence relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every path that places a delivery before its required pickup must omit at least one arc.
assumptions_latex: Pickup and delivery for each request must lie on the same route.
The declared precedence relation is mandatory for every feasible route.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every precedence-violating path \(P\) satisfies \(\sum_{a\in P}x_a\leq |P|-1\).

children.title: Time-Window Inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Window Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc-conditioned service-time propagation inequality for vehicle routing with time windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let customer \(i\) have service-start window \([e_i,\ell_i]\), service duration \(s_i\), and travel time \(t_{ij}\geq0\). With binary arc variable \(x_{ij}\) and service-start variable \(T_i\), define \(M_{ij}=\max\{0,\ell_i+s_i+t_{ij}-e_j\}\). Every feasible schedule satisfies \[e_i\leq T_i\leq\ell_i,\qquad T_j\geq T_i+s_i+t_{ij}-M_{ij}(1-x_{ij}).\] When \(x_{ij}=1\), the second inequality enforces temporal propagation; when \(x_{ij}=0\), the chosen constant makes it redundant over the stated windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting arc i-to-j forces service at j to start after service and travel from i; a valid big-M deactivates the condition otherwise.
assumptions_latex: Travel and service times are deterministic and nonnegative.
\(x_{ij}=1\) means that vertex \(j\) is visited immediately after \(i\) on one route.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed bounds and propagation inequality are valid for every feasible time-window schedule.

children.title: Path–Schedule Coupling Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Path–Schedule Coupling Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-clique cuts coupling selected vehicle paths with mutually incompatible schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be candidate paths, \(S\) candidate schedules, and \(G=(P\cup S,E)\) the conflict graph, where an edge joins two selections that cannot occur together because of timing, precedence, resource, or path-schedule inconsistency. For binary selection variables \(z_p\) and \(w_s\), every clique \(Q\) of \(G\) induces the valid coupling cut
\[
\sum_{p\in Q\cap P}z_p+\sum_{s\in Q\cap S}w_s\le 1.
\]
In particular, an incompatible pair \((p,s)\in E\) yields \(z_p+w_s\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any clique of mutually incompatible path and schedule choices contains at most one selected member, yielding a valid mixed path-schedule inequality.
assumptions_latex: Every edge of \(G\) represents genuine joint infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{p\in Q\cap P}z_p+\sum_{s\in Q\cap S}w_s\le1\) for every clique \(Q\) of \(G\).

notation.meaning: Conflict graph on path and schedule selections.

children.title: Subset-Row Cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Subset-Row Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical odd-cardinality subset-row inequality for a set-partitioning route master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the integer set-partitioning system \(\sum_{r\in R}a_{ir}\lambda_r=1\) for each customer \(i\), where \(a_{ir}\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\lambda_r\in\mathbb Z_+\). For any odd customer subset \(S\) with \(|S|=2k+1\), summing its rows with multiplier \(1/2\) and rounding down produces the valid inequality
\[
\sum_{r\in R}\left\lfloor\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i\in S}a_{ir}\right\rfloor\lambda_r\le k.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an odd customer subset, half-summing its covering rows and rounding gives a valid inequality limiting routes that cover multiple selected customers.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{ir}\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\lambda_r\in\mathbb Z_+\).
\(\sum_{r\in R}a_{ir}\lambda_r=1\) for every customer \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{r\in R}\left\lfloor \frac12\sum_{i\in S}a_{ir}\right\rfloor\lambda_r\le (|S|-1)/2\) for odd \(|S|\).

notation.meaning: Indicator that route r serves customer i.

children.title: Rank-One Cuts
children.top_down_role: Rank-one cutting-plane families used in route-based VRP relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one Chvátal–Gomory cuts for the integer route-master formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\lambda\le\mathbf1\) be valid for every integer route selection \(\lambda\in\mathbb Z_+^{R}\). For any multiplier vector \(u\in\mathbb R_+^{m}\), integrality implies the rank-one Chvátal–Gomory inequality
\[
\sum_{r\in R}\left\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}A_{ullet r}\right\rfloor\lambda_r
\le \left\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1\right\rfloor.
\]
It is rank one because it follows from one nonnegative aggregation of the original rows followed by a single rounding operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative aggregation of valid packing rows, followed by coefficient and right-side rounding, yields a valid rank-one cut for integer route selections.
assumptions_latex: \(A\lambda\le\mathbf1\) is valid for all feasible \(\lambda\in\mathbb Z_+^R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{r\in R}\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}A_{\bullet r}\rfloor\lambda_r\le\lfloor u^{\mathsf T}\mathbf1\rfloor\).

notation.meaning: Column of route r in the customer-route incidence matrix.

review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports rank-one Chvátal–Gomory cuts.

children.title: Subset-Row Rank-One Specializations
children.top_down_role: Specialization, containment, strengthening, plus implementation boundaries linking the two cut families.

knowledge_statements.title: Subset-Row Rank-One Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-multiplier specialization of rank-one cuts on selected customer rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the set-partitioning route master, choose a customer subset \(S\) and an integer \(q\ge2\), and assign multiplier \(u_i=1/q\) for \(i\in S\) and \(u_i=0\) otherwise. The resulting rank-one specialization is
\[
\sum_{r\in R}\left\lfloor\frac{|S\cap C(r)|}{q}\right\rfloor\lambda_r
\le\left\lfloor\frac{|S|}{q}\right\rfloor,
\]
where \(C(r)\) is the customer set served by route \(r\). The classical subset-row cut is the case \(q=2\) with odd \(|S|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform multipliers on selected customer rows produce a family of rank-one cuts; denominator two and odd subset size give the classical subset-row cut.
assumptions_latex: Each customer is covered exactly once by integer route variables.
\(q\in\mathbb Z\) and \(q\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{r\in R}\lfloor |S\cap C(r)|/q\rfloor\lambda_r\le\lfloor |S|/q\rfloor\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports this generalized subset-row specialization.

children.title: Assignment Bounds
children.top_down_role: VRP bounds derived from assignment-based relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound obtained by relaxing routing structure to a minimum-cost assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) contain all customers and enough depot copies to encode the prescribed fleet, and let every feasible routing solution induce a permutation matrix \(x\) on \(U\). Define
\[
L_{\mathrm{AP}}=\min\left\{\sum_{i,j\in U}c_{ij}x_{ij}:\sum_jx_{ij}=1,\ \sum_ix_{ij}=1,\ x_{ij}\ge0\right\}.
\]
Because the assignment model drops route connectivity, capacity, scheduling, and subtour restrictions while retaining every routing incidence vector, \(L_{\mathrm{AP}}\le z_{\mathrm{VRP}}^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping connectivity, capacity, scheduling, and subtour requirements leaves an assignment problem whose optimum is a lower bound on routing cost.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible routing solution admits the stated depot-copy assignment encoding.
Arc costs in the assignment objective equal the corresponding routing costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{AP}}\le z_{\mathrm{VRP}}^*\).

children.title: Spanning-Structure Bounds
children.top_down_role: VRP bounds derived from trees, forests, one-trees, or related spanning structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Spanning-Structure Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-spanning-tree lower bound for nonnegative undirected routing costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected routing graph containing the depot and all customers, with costs \(c_e\ge0\). The union of the edges traversed by any feasible fleet of depot-rooted routes contains a connected spanning subgraph of \(G\). Hence, if
\[
L_{\mathrm{ST}}=\min\left\{\sum_{e\in T}c_e:T\text{ is a spanning tree of }G\right\},
\]
then \(L_{\mathrm{ST}}\le z_{\mathrm{VRP}}^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible depot-rooted fleet connects all vertices, so a minimum spanning tree costs no more than an optimal routing solution.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is undirected and contains every depot and customer vertex.
\(c_e\ge0\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{ST}}\le z_{\mathrm{VRP}}^*\).

notation.meaning: Spanning tree of the routing graph.
