children.title: Assignment–Spanning Hybrid Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds combining assignment restrictions with spanning connectivity structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment–Spanning Hybrid Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection relaxation combining assignment structure with spanning connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_{m A}\) be an assignment relaxation and \(X_{m S}\) a spanning-connectivity relaxation, both containing every feasible routing incidence vector. With the same cost vector \(c\), define
\[
L_{m H}=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X_{m A}\cap X_{m S}\}.
\]
If \(L_{m A}=\min_{x\in X_{m A}}c^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(L_{m S}=\min_{x\in X_{m S}}c^{\mathsf T}x\), then
\[
\max\{L_{m A},L_{m S}\}\le L_{m H}\le z_{m VRP}^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting assignment and spanning relaxations remains a valid lower bound and is at least as strong as either component bound.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible routing incidence vector belongs to both \(X_{m A}\) and \(X_{m S}\).
All three relaxations use the same minimization objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{L_{m A},L_{m S}\}\le L_{m H}\le z_{m VRP}^*\).
review_flags: The dominance statement is standard relaxation logic, but no supplied locator documents this hybrid VRP construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-inclusion argument correctly gives \(\max\{L_{\rm A},L_{\rm S}\}\le L_{\rm H}\le z_{\rm VRP}^*\) under the stated common-variable and common-objective assumptions. Nevertheless, no inspectable source documents this assignment-spanning hybrid construction in the intended VRP context.

children.title: Route-Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds obtained from relaxations expressed over feasible or relaxed routes.

knowledge_statements.title: Route-Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-partitioning linear relaxation over feasible vehicle routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be the set of feasible vehicle routes, let \(c_r\) be route cost, and let \(a_{ir}=1\) when route \(r\) serves customer \(i\). The route-master relaxation is
\[
L_R=\min\left\{\sum_{r\in R}c_r\lambda_r:\sum_{r\in R}a_{ir}\lambda_r=1\ \forall i,\ \lambda_r\ge0\right\},
\]
with any required fleet row included. Replacing \(\lambda_r\ge0\) by \(\lambda_r\in\mathbb Z_+\) recovers the route-selection model; therefore \(L_R\le z_{m VRP}^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing integrality in the feasible-route set-partitioning master gives a lower bound on the minimum routing cost.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) contains every route allowed by the VRP.
The integer route master exactly represents feasible fleet solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_R\le z_{m VRP}^*\).

notation.meaning: Continuous route-use variable in the relaxation.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the VRP route-master relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The route-master LP relaxation is stated coherently and property is the correct role for a bound-family leaf. No citation with a specific locator supports the exact VRP set-partitioning formulation, including the optional fleet row and exactness assumption.

children.title: Column-Generation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds obtained through dynamically generated route columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasibility certificate for the full route-master LP bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the route master with customer equalities and route costs \(c_r\), let \(\pi_i\) be unrestricted customer-row dual prices and include analogous prices for any fleet rows. If exact pricing verifies
\[
\bar c_r=c_r-\sum_i a_{ir}\pi_i\ge0\qquad\text{for every }r\in R,
\]
then \(\pi\) is feasible for the full master dual. Its dual objective \(D(\pi)=\sum_i\pi_i\), augmented by fleet-row terms when present, satisfies \(D(\pi)\le L_R\le z_{m VRP}^*\). Equality with the restricted-master value certifies optimality of the full route relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact pricing that finds no negative reduced-cost route makes the dual prices feasible and certifies the full route-relaxation bound.
assumptions_latex: Pricing is exact over the complete feasible-route set \(R\).
The displayed reduced cost includes every master-row dual contribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(\pi)\le L_R\le z_{m VRP}^*\), with equality to the restricted-master value at full LP optimality.

notation.meaning: Dual price for customer i's master row.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically documents column-generation dual certificates for the VRP route master.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual-feasibility certificate is standard and certificate is the appropriate content kind, but no source is supplied. The displayed reduced-cost formula includes only customer-row contributions while the prose allows fleet rows; a sourced replacement should display all applicable dual contributions explicitly.

children.title: Restricted-Master Bound Progression
children.top_down_role: Bound evolution as route columns enlarge or refine a restricted master.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Bound Progression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic objective progression as route columns are added to a minimization master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R_1\subseteq R_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq R\), and let \(v_k\) be the optimal value of the continuous route master restricted to columns in \(R_k\). Whenever each restricted master is feasible,
\[
v_1\ge v_2\ge\cdots\ge L_R.
\]
If some \(R_K\) contains an optimal solution's positive columns, then \(v_K=L_R\). Before a full-dual feasibility certificate is obtained by pricing, \(v_k\) is an upper bound on \(L_R\), not necessarily a valid lower bound on the integer VRP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding route columns can only decrease the restricted-master value toward the full LP optimum; intermediate values need not lower-bound the integer problem.
assumptions_latex: \(R_k\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R\).
Every considered restricted master is feasible and has the same rows and objective coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_k\ge v_{k+1}\ge L_R\), with equality once the retained columns support a full-master optimum.

notation.meaning: Route columns present at iteration k.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports restricted-master progression.
Important bound-direction distinction requires domain-specific source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotone decrease of feasible restricted-master objective values and the warning that they need not lower-bound the integer VRP optimum are mathematically consistent. No inspectable source supports this progression in the route-master setting, so the domain-specific bound interpretation remains unsourced.

children.title: Lagrangian Bounds
children.top_down_role: VRP bounds obtained through multiplier-based relaxation of selected requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds from dualizing complicating constraints in a minimization VRP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the minimization problem as \(z^*=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ Ax\ge b\}\), where \(X\) retains the remaining routing restrictions. For every multiplier \(u\ge0\), define
\[
L(u)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(c^{\mathsf T}x+u^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\bigr).
\]
For every feasible \(x\), the penalty term is nonpositive, so \(L(u)\le z^*\). The Lagrangian dual bound is \(L^*=\sup_{u\ge0}L(u)\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers move complicating inequalities into the objective; maximizing the resulting relaxation value gives a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is a minimization problem with constraints \(Ax\ge b\).
\(u\ge0\), and \(L(u)\) is well-defined in the extended real line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(u)\le L^*\le z^*\) for every \(u\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Domain retaining the nondualized routing restrictions.

children.title: Surrogate Bounds
children.top_down_role: VRP bounds obtained by aggregating selected requirements into surrogate restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained by nonnegative aggregation of complicating inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z^*=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ Ax\ge b\}\) and any \(u\ge0\), replace all rows of \(Ax\ge b\) by the single surrogate constraint \(u^{\mathsf T}Ax\ge u^{\mathsf T}b\). Define
\[
S(u)=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ u^{\mathsf T}Ax\ge u^{\mathsf T}b\}.
\]
Every feasible solution of the original problem satisfies the aggregated constraint; hence \(S(u)\le z^*\), and \(S^*=\sup_{u\ge0}S(u)\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted aggregation of valid inequalities enlarges the feasible region, so its optimum and the best such value are lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: The original problem minimizes \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\) and \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(u)\le S^*\le z^*\) for every \(u\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Best surrogate bound over nonnegative multipliers.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports surrogate relaxation bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonnegative aggregation produces a relaxation and therefore a valid lower bound with the stated direction. Property fits the bound-family leaf, but no source reference or specific locator was supplied for surrogate relaxation bounds.

children.title: Multiplier-Aggregation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Bound strength, separability, plus computational tradeoffs across multiplier or aggregation regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Aggregation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and strength tradeoff for nonnegative aggregation of routing-model inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) contain the remaining VRP constraints, and consider \(z=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X,\ Ax\ge b\}\). For any multiplier vector \(\lambda\ge0\), define the aggregated relaxation \(z(\lambda)=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X,\ \lambda^\top Ax\ge\lambda^\top b\}\). Every feasible solution of the original problem is feasible for this relaxation, so \(z(\lambda)\le z\). If an aggregation retains several inequalities \(\Lambda Ax\ge\Lambda b\), then adding rows to \(\Lambda\) cannot decrease its minimization bound. Thus fewer aggregate rows reduce relaxation size but may weaken the bound; optimizing over a larger admissible multiplier family cannot worsen the best obtainable bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative aggregation preserves bound validity. Keeping more aggregate inequalities or optimizing over more multipliers can strengthen the bound, at the cost of a larger relaxation or multiplier search.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and the displayed minima are well-defined.
\(Ax\ge b\) is satisfied by every feasible VRP solution.
\(\lambda\ge0\), or every row of \(\Lambda\) is componentwise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z(\lambda)\le z\), with monotone bound strength under enlargement of the retained aggregation or multiplier family.

notation.meaning: Set defined by all constraints not being aggregated.
Nonnegative aggregation multiplier vector or matrix.
Optimal value of the aggregated minimization relaxation.

review_flags: VRP-specific multiplier-aggregation source and locator required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is mathematically sound and fits the tradeoff container, but no inspectable source supports the multiplier-aggregation formulation or its monotonicity claims.

children.title: Pricing-Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that the relevant pricing search cannot produce an improving route column.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact column-generation certificate for a finite route-based master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\sum_{r\in R}c_rx_r:\sum_{r\in R}a_rx_r=b,\ x\ge0\}\), and let \(R'\subseteq R\) be the restricted columns. A pricing-optimality certificate consists of a restricted-master feasible solution \(x'\), a vector \(\pi\), and an exact pricing result \(\rho=\min_{r\in R}(c_r-a_r^\top\pi)\). It is valid when \(a_r^\top\pi\le c_r\) for every \(r\in R'\), \(\rho\ge0\), and \(\sum_{r\in R'}c_rx'_r=b^\top\pi\). Then \(\pi\) is feasible for the full dual, and equality of primal and dual objectives certifies that \(x'\) is optimal for the full master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted solution is globally LP-optimal when its dual vector is restricted-dual feasible, exact pricing finds no negative reduced-cost route, and the primal and dual objectives agree.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite and the full master LP is feasible with a finite optimum.
The pricing computation attains the minimum reduced cost over all admissible routes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x'\) is optimal for the full route-based master LP.

notation.meaning: Dual vector for the master equalities.
Minimum reduced cost over all admissible routes.

children.title: Dual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual evidence supporting a relaxation bound or master-problem optimality claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak- and strong-duality certificates for a route-based master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the master LP \(P=\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), any vector \(\pi\) satisfying \(A^\top\pi\le c\) is a dual certificate: every primal-feasible \(x\) obeys \(b^\top\pi=\pi^\top Ax\le c^\top x\). Hence \(b^\top\pi\) is a verifiable lower bound on \(P\). If a primal-feasible \(\bar x\) additionally satisfies \(c^\top\bar x=b^\top\pi\), then \((\bar x,\pi)\) is an optimality certificate. Equivalently, equality follows when every column used positively by \(\bar x\) has zero reduced cost \(c_j-A_j^\top\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible vector supplies a lower bound. Together with a feasible route solution of equal objective value, it certifies LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(b\), and \(c\) are finite-dimensional real data.
\(\bar x\ge0\) and \(A\bar x=b\) when optimality is claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^\top\pi\le P\); if \(c^\top\bar x=b^\top\pi\), then \(\bar x\) and \(\pi\) are primal-dual optimal.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the route-based master minimization LP.
Dual certificate for the equality constraints.
Column of the master matrix associated with route variable j.

children.title: Pricing–Dual Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements linking pricing evidence to the dual state of the route master.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing–Dual Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition linking route pricing to full-master dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For master columns \((a_r,c_r)\), a dual vector \(\pi\), and an exact pricing oracle, define \(\bar c_r=c_r-a_r^\top\pi\) and let the oracle return \(r^*\in\arg\min_{r\in R}\bar c_r\). Pricing and the dual are consistent precisely when the oracle uses the same costs, column coefficients, dual signs, and route set as the master. Under this condition, \(\bar c_{r^*}\ge0\) if and only if \(a_r^\top\pi\le c_r\) for every \(r\in R\). Thus absence of a negative reduced-cost route is exactly full-master dual feasibility, rather than merely feasibility over the restricted columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact pricing is dual-consistent when it uses identical master data and conventions; then no negative reduced-cost route is equivalent to feasibility of every full-master dual constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is finite and nonempty.
The pricing oracle returns a global minimizer over exactly \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{r\in R}(c_r-a_r^\top\pi)\ge0\iff A^\top\pi\le c\).

notation.meaning: Complete set of admissible master routes.

children.title: Cut-Separation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence concerning violation searches or separation completeness for specified cut families.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Separation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable positive certificate for separating a fractional VRP relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in Q:\alpha_i^\top x\le\beta_i\text{ for every }i\in I\}\) be a cut-strengthened VRP relaxation, and let \(\bar x\in Q\). A positive cut-separation certificate is a triple \((i,\alpha_i,\beta_i)\) accompanied by checkable data establishing \(i\in I\), such that \(\alpha_i^\top\bar x>\beta_i\). Membership in the declared valid-inequality family establishes that every \(x\in P\) satisfies the cut, while the strict displayed inequality establishes that \(\bar x\notin P\). The certificate verifies discovery of a violated cut; it does not by itself certify that no other violated cut exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid family member whose evaluated left side exceeds its right side certifies separation of the relaxation point, but does not certify exhaustive separation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in Q\).
Every indexed inequality \(\alpha_i^\top x\le\beta_i\) is valid for the intended relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_i^\top\bar x>\beta_i\) certifies \(\bar x\notin P\).

notation.meaning: Base VRP relaxation before the indexed cut family.
Index set of the declared valid-cut family.

children.title: Relaxation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting the value, feasibility status, or solved state of a VRP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for the value of a finite VRP LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write a VRP relaxation in equality standard form as \(P=\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\). A relaxation-value certificate is a pair \((\bar x,\bar\pi)\) satisfying \(A\bar x=b\), \(\bar x\ge0\), \(A^\top\bar\pi\le c\), and \(c^\top\bar x=b^\top\bar\pi\). All conditions are directly checkable from the relaxation data. Primal feasibility gives \(P\le c^\top\bar x\), dual feasibility gives \(b^\top\bar\pi\le P\), and objective equality identifies their common value as \(P\). This certifies the relaxation bound, not integrality or feasibility for the original integer VRP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching feasible primal and dual LP solutions certify the exact relaxation value, but do not establish integer feasibility or integer optimality.
assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional relaxation is represented exactly in the displayed standard form.
Its coefficients and certificate entries can be checked without numerical ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=c^\top\bar x=b^\top\bar\pi\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the VRP LP relaxation.

children.title: Separation–Relaxation Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between active cuts, separation status, plus the certified relaxation state.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation–Relaxation Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring a solved working relaxation matches the full cut relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=Q\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}\{x:\alpha_i^\top x\le\beta_i\}\) and let \(J\subseteq I\) define the working relaxation \(P_J\). For minimization, suppose \(\bar x\) is certified optimal over \(P_J\), and an exact separator certifies \(\alpha_i^\top\bar x\le\beta_i\) for every \(i\in I\). Then \(P\subseteq P_J\) and \(\bar x\in P\). Consequently, \(\min_{x\in P_J}c^\top x\le\min_{x\in P}c^\top x\le c^\top\bar x=\min_{x\in P_J}c^\top x\). Thus the working-relaxation certificate and exhaustive separation result consistently certify optimality over the full cut relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a working-relaxation optimum violates no inequality in the complete cut family, it is also optimal for the full cut relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(J\subseteq I\), and both relaxations use the same base set \(Q\) and objective \(c\).
The separator is exact over the complete family \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in P}c^\top x\) and \(\min_{x\in P}c^\top x=\min_{x\in P_J}c^\top x\).

notation.meaning: Working relaxation containing only cuts indexed by J.
Certified optimum of the working relaxation.

children.title: Branching-Exhaustion Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that all relevant branches have been resolved or excluded.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Exhaustion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite branch-and-bound certificate that all residual integer possibilities are covered and closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization VRP with integer-feasible set \(F\), a branching-exhaustion certificate is a finite rooted tree. Each internal node has children whose branching regions cover its region's integer points. Each leaf \(v\) carries either a verifiable proof that \(F\cap R_v=\varnothing\), or a valid lower bound \(L_v\) on \(\min\{c^\top x:x\in F\cap R_v\}\). Given an incumbent \(x^I\in F\) with value \(U=c^\top x^I\), the tree is exhausted when every leaf is certified infeasible or has \(L_v\ge U\). Coverage then implies that no feasible integer solution has value below \(U\), so the incumbent is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite branching tree certifies optimality when its leaves cover every integer solution and each leaf is either infeasible or bounded no better than the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the intended integer-feasible VRP set.
Every branch disjunction covers all integer points in its parent region.
Every leaf infeasibility proof or lower bound is independently valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^I\in\arg\min_{x\in F}c^\top x\).

notation.meaning: Branching region associated with tree node v.
Certified lower bound at leaf v.
Objective value of the feasible incumbent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-tree coverage and leaf-closure conditions form an appropriate branch-and-bound optimality certificate, but the record supplies no inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Optimality-Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting an absolute or relative gap between incumbent value plus valid bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and relative minimization-gap certificate from an incumbent and global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\min_{x\in F}c^\top x\). An optimality-gap certificate consists of a feasible incumbent \(x^I\in F\) with \(U=c^\top x^I\) and a verifiable global lower bound \(L\le z^*\). It certifies \(L\le z^*\le U\), hence absolute suboptimality \(0\le U-z^*\le U-L\). For a declared scale \(D>0\), it also certifies scaled relative gap at most \((U-L)/D\). Choosing \(D=\max\{1,|U|\}\) fixes a convention that remains defined when \(U=0\). If \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal in absolute objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent and valid global lower bound bracket the optimum; their difference certifies an absolute gap and, after declaring a positive scale, a relative gap.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) and \(z^*\) is finite.
Feasibility of \(x^I\) and validity of \(L\) are independently certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le U-z^*\le U-L\); if \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), then \(U\le z^*+\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Objective value of the feasible incumbent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The absolute-gap statement and explicitly scaled relative-gap convention are mathematically precise and correctly classified as a certificate, but no source is cited.

children.title: Tree–Gap Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency among node statuses, global bounds, incumbent values, plus reported termination status.

assumptions_latex: The active leaves cover every feasible solution capable of improving the incumbent.
Each \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for its complete leaf subproblem.
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_T\le z^*\le U\), and the certified absolute gap is \(U-L_T\).

notation.meaning: Set of active leaves in the branching tree.
Incumbent-clamped global lower bound derived from the active-leaf bounds.
Objective value of a feasible incumbent.

global tree bound clamped by incumbent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition linking active branch-tree leaf bounds to a reported global gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=\min_{x\in F}c^\top x\), where \(F\) is the integer-feasible set, and let the active leaves \(V\) of a valid branching tree cover every feasible solution with objective value below the feasible incumbent value \(U\). For each \(v\in V\), let \(L_v\) be a valid lower bound for the leaf subproblem, and define \(L_T=\min\bigl(\{U\}\cup\{L_v:v\in V\}\bigr)\). A reported global lower bound \(L\) is tree-consistent when \(L\le L_T\), and it is tight with respect to the stored leaf bounds and incumbent when \(L=L_T\). Then \(L_T\le z^*\le U\), so the tree-certified absolute gap is \(U-L_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tree's certified global lower bound is the minimum of the incumbent value and all valid active-leaf bounds. Subtracting this clamped bound from the incumbent gives the tree-certified absolute gap.

children.title: Route-Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that a candidate route or required route structure cannot be feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Route-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-structural certificate that a proposed customer sequence cannot form an admissible route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be the directed routing graph, with depot \(0\), and let \(s=(0,v_1,\ldots,v_k,0)\) be a proposed route sequence. A route-infeasibility certificate is an index \(j\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\) such that the consecutive arc \((v_j,v_{j+1})\notin A\), where \(v_0=v_{k+1}=0\). Verification requires only membership testing in \(A\). Because a route realizing \(s\) must traverse every consecutive arc, the missing arc proves that \(s\) is not a route in \(G\), independently of capacity, time-window, or other resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missing arc between consecutive vertices of a proposed depot-to-depot sequence certifies that the sequence is not a route in the routing graph.
assumptions_latex: Admissible route movements are exactly the arcs in \(A\).
The proposed route must follow the displayed vertex order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((v_j,v_{j+1})\notin A\) certifies that \(s\) is route-infeasible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A missing consecutive arc is a valid graph-structural route-infeasibility witness, and the scope correctly excludes resource infeasibility. No source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Resource-Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that time, load, energy, or another resource restriction cannot be satisfied.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-based certificate that a customer set cannot be served by one vehicle route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a vehicle have capacity \(Q\ge0\), and let each customer \(i\) have nonnegative indivisible demand \(d_i\). For a set \(S\) required to be served by one route without replenishment or split delivery, the data \(S\) and its demand sum form a resource-infeasibility certificate whenever \(\sum_{i\in S}d_i>Q\). Every route serving all customers in \(S\) must carry their total demand, while its load cannot exceed \(Q\). Therefore no capacity-feasible single route can contain all of \(S\). The certificate concerns joint service on one route and does not imply infeasibility of serving \(S\) with multiple vehicles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the total indivisible demand of customers assigned to one non-replenishing route exceeds vehicle capacity, that assignment is resource-infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(d_i\ge0\) for every customer \(i\in S\).
One vehicle of capacity \(Q\) must serve all of \(S\) without replenishment or split delivery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in S}d_i>Q\) certifies that no capacity-feasible single route serves all customers in \(S\).

notation.meaning: Customer set required on one route.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The capacity-overload witness is correct under the stated no-replenishment and no-split-delivery assumptions and fits the certificate container, but it lacks an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Route–Resource Conflict Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence localizing infeasibility to interactions between route structure plus resource limits.

assumptions_latex: A finite customer set and a finite family of depot-to-depot routes are given.
Each route has a resource-consumption vector, and feasibility is defined by componentwise resource limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conflict is a polynomially checkable certificate that no feasible solution can contain all routes in \(Q\).

notation.meaning: consumption of resource k by route r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers additive fleet or depot resources shared by otherwise feasible routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be a finite set of individually feasible routes. A route–resource conflict certificate is a pair \((Q,k)\) such that resource \(k\) has capacity \(b_k\), each \(r\in Q\) consumes \(a_{kr}\ge 0\), and \[\sum_{r\in Q} a_{kr}>b_k.\] For binary route-selection variables \(y_r\), every feasible fleet solution therefore satisfies \[\sum_{r\in Q}y_r\le |Q|-1.\] Verification consists only of checking the route identities, the recorded consumptions, and the displayed strict inequality. The certificate establishes joint infeasibility without asserting that any individual route in \(Q\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routes form a verifiable conflict when their combined consumption exceeds a shared resource limit; consequently, at least one route must be excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Route–Resource Conflict Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a binary routing variable \(x_e\) with \(0<x_e^*<1\). The standard two-way branching structure replaces the parent region \(P\) by \[P_0=P\cap\{x:x_e=0\},\qquad P_1=P\cap\{x:x_e=1\}.\] Because every integer-feasible routing vector has \(x_e\in\{0,1\}\), its feasible set is partitioned between the two children, whereas the fractional vector \(x^*\) belongs to neither. knowledge_statements.title: VRP Node-Bounding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention; maximization reverses the bound inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\in\mathbb R^m\) be the objective vector and let \(X_N\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be the integer-feasible set at node \(N\). For a relaxation \(R\supseteq X_N\), define \[L_N(R)=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in R\},\qquad z_N^*=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in X_N\},\] using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \(L_N(R)\le z_N^*\). If \(X_N\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\), then \[L_N(R_1)\le L_N(R_2)\le z_N^*.\] Thus tightening a valid node relaxation cannot decrease its lower bound for a minimization VRP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid node relaxation gives a lower bound, and tightening the relaxation cannot decrease that bound in a minimization VRP.

children.title: VRP Fathoming Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural bases for closing nodes through bounds, feasibility status, or dominance.

knowledge_statements.title: VRP Fathoming Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard exact fathoming rules for a finite minimization VRP search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) define the minimization objective, let \(U\) be the incumbent value, and let \(L_N\) be a certified lower bound for node \(N\). The node may be fathomed if: its feasible set \(X_N\) is certified empty; \(L_N\ge U\); or the relaxation optimum is attained by an integer-feasible point \(\bar x\in X_N\) satisfying \(c^\top\bar x=L_N\). In the third case first update \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,c^\top\bar x\}\). Each condition permits closing the node without discarding an integer solution having objective value below the updated incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A VRP node may be closed after certified infeasibility, bound dominance by the incumbent, or attainment of the node bound by an integer-feasible relaxation solution.
assumptions_latex: A finite minimization branch-and-bound search is used.
\(c\) defines the objective \(c^\top x\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified infeasibility, \(L_N\ge U\), or an integer-feasible relaxation optimizer attaining \(L_N\) is sufficient to fathom node \(N\).

children.title: VRP State-Space Search

knowledge_statements.title: VRP State-Space Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact label search on a finite acyclic route-state graph with continuation-preserving dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(\mathcal S,A)\) be a finite acyclic state graph with source state \(s_0\) and terminal set \(T\). Initialize the open set with a label \(\ell_0\) at \(s_0\), where \(g(\ell_0)=0\). Repeatedly remove an open label \(\ell\) and create a successor for every feasible transition \((s(\ell),s')\in A\), updating its resources and cost. A label may be discarded only if a retained label at the same state has no greater accumulated cost and can reproduce every feasible continuation of the discarded label with no greater incremental cost. When no open labels remain, return a least-cost terminal label and recover its route through predecessor pointers; if no terminal label exists, report infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact state-space search expands labels on a finite acyclic route graph and discards a label only under continuation-preserving dominance.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(\mathcal S,A)\) is a finite acyclic directed graph representing partial VRP routes.
Every represented feasible route corresponds to an \(s_0\)-to-\(T\) path, and path cost equals route cost.
The dominance test preserves all feasible continuations and does not increase their incremental costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite label search returns a minimum-cost represented route or correctly reports that no represented feasible route exists.

children.title: State Aggregation Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: State Aggregation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between continuation-preserving and potentially lossy aggregation of partial-route histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Call two partial routes \(p\) and \(q\) continuation-equivalent when \(\mathcal C(p)=\mathcal C(q)\) and every common continuation has the same incremental cost from both histories. An aggregation map \(\alpha\) is continuation preserving if \(\alpha(p)=\alpha(q)\) only for continuation-equivalent histories. Such aggregation preserves all completion values, including \(J(p)=J(q)\), and therefore preserves the represented optimum. If two merged histories differ in continuation feasibility or incremental cost, the aggregation is potentially lossy and can change the optimum, although it need not do so in every instance. For elementary routing, retaining only current vertex and load while omitting the visited set can merge histories for which a customer-revisiting continuation is feasible from only one history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging continuation-equivalent histories is exact; merging histories with different feasible continuations or continuation costs can make route-state aggregation lossy.
assumptions_latex: Partial routes are mapped to aggregate states by \(\alpha\).
\(\mathcal C(p)\) is the feasible-continuation set of partial route \(p\).
\(J(p)\) is the minimum completion cost from partial route \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Continuation-preserving aggregation preserves the represented optimum, whereas merging histories with different continuation behavior can change it.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate cost \(c_r\) and binary variable \(y_r\) with every route \(r\in\mathcal R\). The route-master representation is \[\min\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}c_ry_r\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}a_{ir}y_r=1\ \text{for every customer }i,\quad \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}y_r\le K,\quad y_r\in\{0,1\}.\] Each feasible selection partitions the customers among at most \(K\) feasible routes. Conversely, every feasible VRP solution whose routes belong to \(\mathcal R\) defines a feasible binary vector of equal cost. Thus the formulation is exact when \(\mathcal R\) contains every admissible route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting complete feasible routes in a set-partitioning model exactly represents the VRP when every admissible route is included.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\) and a search list containing the empty depot-rooted partial route. Remove a partial route \(p\); for each unserved customer whose insertion preserves all route constraints, generate the extended route and add it to the search list. Whenever returning to the depot produces a feasible nonempty route \(r\), insert \(r\) into \(\mathcal R\). Continue until the list is empty, using only pruning rules proved unable to remove a feasible route. Construct the exact binary route-master model over \(\mathcal R\), solve it to integer optimality, and output its selected routes. Report infeasibility if the master has no feasible binary solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The enumeration–master interface maps each feasible route \(r\) to a column \((a_r,c_r)\), where \((a_r)_i=1\) exactly when \(r\) serves customer \(i\). knowledge_statements.title: VRP Branching Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact branching over a finite VRP search tree using covering disjunctions and valid fathoming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the open set \(\mathcal O\) with the root VRP node. Select a node, solve its relaxation, and close it if a valid fathoming criterion applies. If the relaxation optimizer \(x^*\) is integer feasible, update the incumbent and close the node. Otherwise choose a finite disjunction \(D_1\vee\cdots\vee D_q\) that is satisfied by every integer-feasible solution of the node and for which \(x^*\) violates every disjunct. Create child \(j\) by adding \(D_j\), retain all valid inherited constraints, and add every nonfathomed child to \(\mathcal O\). Under the assumption that this process generates a finite tree, repeat until \(\mathcal O=\varnothing\), then return the best verified integer solution or report infeasibility if none was found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process a finite VRP search tree by valid fathoming, incumbent updates, and branching disjunctions whose children cover every integer solution.

Every branching disjunction covers all integer-feasible solutions of its parent and excludes the selected fractional optimizer from every child.
All node bounds and fathoming decisions are valid.

knowledge_statements.title: VRP Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-shot separation over a specified finite family of valid VRP inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a finite index set for valid inequalities \(a(u)^\top x\le b(u)\), and let \(x^*\) satisfy the current relaxation. For each \(u\in U\), compute \(v(u)=a(u)^\top x^*-b(u)\), and choose \(u^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in U}v(u)\). If \(v(u^*)>0\), return the violated valid inequality \(a(u^*)^\top x\le b(u^*)\). Otherwise certify that \(x^*\) satisfies every inequality in this family. For \(U=\varnothing\), return the latter certificate immediately. This certificate concerns only the selected family and does not establish membership in the integer VRP polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact separation over a finite VRP inequality family returns a maximally violated member or certifies that the current point satisfies the entire family.

\(U\) is a finite index set.

children.title: Tree–Cut Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interactions among branching decisions, cut validity, cut management, plus node processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree–Cut Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-cut coordination for a finite route-based VRP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an active-node set \(\mathcal N\) containing a root relaxation, repeatedly select \(v\in\mathcal N\), solve its current LP relaxation, and separate every available valid inequality violated by the LP solution. Add selected cuts locally or globally and reoptimize until no selected separator returns a violation. Fathom \(v\) if its relaxation is infeasible, integral, or has objective value no better than the incumbent bound. Otherwise choose a branching disjunction whose children partition the integer solutions feasible at \(v\), create those children with all applicable global cuts and inherited local cuts, and insert them into \(\mathcal N\). Stop when \(\mathcal N=\varnothing\); return the incumbent as optimal, or report infeasibility if none exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each search node, separate cuts to closure, fathom when justified, and otherwise branch into exhaustive children while consistently inheriting applicable cuts.
assumptions_latex: The VRP has a finite set of integer-feasible solutions and a valid initial LP relaxation.
Every added inequality is valid for the integer solutions in its declared local or global scope.
Each branching disjunction exhaustively partitions the node's remaining integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the incumbent is globally optimal, or the original VRP is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Core
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master column generation for a finite route-based VRP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be the feasible-route set, with route cost \(c_r\) and master column \(a_r\). Initialize a restricted set \(P\subseteq\mathcal R\) for which the restricted master is feasible. Repeatedly solve the restricted master LP and obtain dual vector \(\pi\). Solve the pricing problem \(\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\bar c_r\), where \(\bar c_r=c_r-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_r\), including any dual contribution from side constraints. If its optimum is negative, add at least one negative-reduced-cost route to \(P\) and repeat. Otherwise stop and return the restricted-master solution, which is optimal for the full master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate restricted-master optimization and minimum-reduced-cost route pricing until no improving route exists; the resulting solution solves the full master relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The full master is a finite minimization LP and the initialized restricted master is feasible.
Pricing returns a globally minimum reduced-cost feasible route.
The dual vector and reduced costs include every current master constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\bar c_r\ge 0\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master LP.
review_flags: Supplied locators concern network duality but do not directly document VRP column generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for branching inside route-based column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a branch-and-price node defined by a branching restriction \(B\) on route-incidence solutions. The restriction is pricing-compatible if there exist a modified feasible-route family \(\mathcal R(B)\) and computable reduced-cost function \(\bar c_r(B,\pi)\) such that: every integer solution satisfying \(B\) decomposes into routes in \(\mathcal R(B)\); every master solution using only \(\mathcal R(B)\) satisfies \(B\); and the oracle can compute \(\min_{r\in\mathcal R(B)}\bar c_r(B,\pi)\) exactly. A branching scheme is pricing-compatible when every child restriction has this property and the children jointly cover all integer solutions at their parent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch is compatible when it can be enforced exactly in both the route master and pricing oracle, while its children exhaust the parent’s integer solutions.
assumptions_latex: Routes are the columns of the node's master formulation.
The pricing oracle is required to certify the minimum reduced cost exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Column generation remains an exact node-relaxation method under every pricing-compatible child restriction \(B\).

notation.meaning: branching restriction at a search node

review_flags: A source formalizing VRP pricing-compatible branching is required.

children.title: Dual Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization families governing dual behavior during route-column generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of dual iterates in route column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_P(\pi)\) denote the restricted-master dual objective over its dual-feasible region \(\Pi_P\), and let \(\pi^c\) be a stabilization center. For parameter \(\rho>0\), compute \(\pi^k\in\arg\max_{\pi\in\Pi_P}\{D_P(\pi)-\tfrac{\rho}{2}\lVert\pi-\pi^c\rVert_2^2\}\). Price routes using \(\pi^k\) and add any certified negative-reduced-cost columns. Update \(\pi^c\) according to a declared serious-step rule when sufficient dual progress occurs; otherwise retain the center and adjust \(\rho\). Terminate only after pricing with a dual vector feasible for the unstabilized full-master dual certifies that every omitted route has nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalize dual movement around a center to reduce oscillation, but terminate only with an unstabilized full-master reduced-cost certificate.
assumptions_latex: Each stabilized restricted-dual subproblem is solved exactly.
Pricing evaluates reduced costs consistently with the dual vector supplied to it.
The final test uses a dual-feasible vector for the unstabilized master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilization changes the search trajectory but not the validity of the final full-master optimality certificate.
review_flags: The precise stabilization variant and authoritative VRP locator are unsupplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind is appropriate, but this particular proximal stabilization model, serious-step update, and unstabilized termination protocol are not supported by a cited source.

children.title: Column-Pool Management
children.top_down_role: Retention, deletion, reactivation, plus organization regimes for generated route columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Pool Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe active-pool control for finite route-based column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an active route set \(P_k\) and an archive \(H_k\). After solving the restricted master and pricing at iteration \(k\), insert every selected negative-reduced-cost route into \(P_{k+1}\). A route may be moved from \(P_k\) to \(H_{k+1}\) when a declared inactivity or reduced-cost rule holds, provided columns needed for restricted-master feasibility are retained. Before invoking exact pricing, optionally reactivate archived routes having negative reduced cost under the current dual vector. Pool deletion or archiving must not be interpreted as eliminating a route from the full set \(\mathcal R\). Stop only when exact pricing over all of \(\mathcal R\), not merely the pool, returns no negative-reduced-cost route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add improving routes, archive dispensable inactive ones, preserve restricted-master feasibility, and certify termination by pricing the full route space rather than the stored pool.
assumptions_latex: The full feasible-route set \(\mathcal R\) is unchanged by pool operations.
Exact full-space pricing remains available for the termination test.
The active restricted master remains feasible after any archival step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pool management preserves exact column-generation optimality when termination is certified over \(\mathcal R\).

notation.meaning: active column pool at iteration k

review_flags: No supplied source directly supports exact VRP column-pool management.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pool-management algorithm is internally coherent and preserves full-space pricing conceptually, but no source supports the stated VRP-specific archival and reactivation protocol.

children.title: Stabilization–Pool Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization–Pool Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled dual-center and route-pool updates in stabilized column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), solve the stabilized restricted master on active pool \(P_k\) to obtain dual vector \(\pi^k\). First rescore archived routes under \(\pi^k\) and reactivate every selected route with negative reduced cost; then invoke exact full-space pricing if reactivation alone does not establish progress. Add generated routes to \(P_k\), reoptimize, and move the stabilization center only after a serious-step test based on the reoptimized dual objective. Archive routes only after this test, retaining feasibility-supporting columns. Regardless of pool and center updates, declare closure only when an unstabilized dual-feasible vector yields nonnegative reduced cost for every route in the full route set \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use stabilized duals to rescore archived routes, update the center after verified progress, and retain a full-space unstabilized termination test.
assumptions_latex: Archived and newly generated routes are evaluated with the same current dual convention.
Exact pricing over \(\mathcal R\) is available.
Archival never destroys restricted-master feasibility.

children.title: Route Pricing Phase
children.top_down_role: The column-generation portion responsible for identifying relevant route structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Route Pricing Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost route search for a route-based VRP master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given master dual vector \(\pi\), construct the resource-constrained route problem whose feasible paths are precisely the routes \(r\in\mathcal R_v\) allowed at the current search node \(v\), including capacity, elementarity or its declared relaxation, branching restrictions, and pricing-compatible cut terms. Compute \(r^\star\in\arg\min_{r\in\mathcal R_v}\bar c_r(\pi)\). If \(\bar c_{r^\star}(\pi)<0\), return one or more negative-reduced-cost routes for insertion into the restricted master. Otherwise return the certificate \(\min_{r\in\mathcal R_v}\bar c_r(\pi)\ge0\). Any heuristic pricing pass may find columns but cannot issue this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the node’s resource-constrained minimum-reduced-cost route problem; add improving routes or certify that none exists using exact, not heuristic, pricing.
assumptions_latex: The pricing model represents exactly the declared node-level route family \(\mathcal R_v\).
All master dual contributions are included in \(\bar c_r(\pi)\).
The certification pass solves pricing globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The phase either supplies an improving route or certifies nonnegative reduced cost over \(\mathcal R_v\).

children.title: Route-Pool Enumeration
children.top_down_role: The retained or explicitly expanded route collection used after pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Route-Pool Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold enumeration of feasible routes after a pricing phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a search node \(v\), dual vector \(\pi\), and threshold \(\tau\ge0\). Traverse an exact resource-feasible route-enumeration search whose leaves represent routes in \(\mathcal R_v\). Maintain for every partial route a valid lower bound on the minimum reduced cost of any feasible completion, and prune a partial route only when infeasible or when this bound exceeds \(\tau\). Insert each completed route \(r\) satisfying \(\bar c_r(\pi)\le	au\) into the pool \(E(\pi,	au)\), suppressing duplicates. Terminate after the finite search is exhausted and return \(E(\pi,	au)=\{r\in\mathcal R_v:\bar c_r(\pi)\le	au\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate exactly all node-feasible routes below a reduced-cost threshold using valid completion bounds, resource pruning, and duplicate suppression.
assumptions_latex: The node-feasible route family \(\mathcal R_v\) is finite.
Completion bounds never exceed the best attainable completion reduced cost.
Resource-feasibility tests and route deduplication are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned pool contains every and only route \(r\in\mathcal R_v\) with \(\bar c_r(\pi)\le	au\).

children.title: Enumeration-Based Closure
children.top_down_role: Exact-search regimes completed over a certified or sufficiently bounded route pool.

knowledge_statements.title: Enumeration-Based Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-pool certificate for closing a route-based search-node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search node \(v\), let \(E\subseteq\mathcal R_v\) be an enumerated route set and solve the master restricted to \(E\), obtaining primal value \(z_E\) and dual vector \(\pi_E\). Enumeration-based closure is certified if the enumeration procedure proves either \(E=\mathcal R_v\) or, more generally, \(\bar c_r(\pi_E)\ge0\) for every omitted route \(r\in\mathcal R_v\setminus E\). Then \(\pi_E\) is feasible for the full node-master dual, so the restricted primal and full dual have the common value \(z_E\). Consequently \(z_E\) is the exact LP bound at \(v\), and ordinary integrality or bound-dominance tests may close the node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted route pool closes the LP relaxation when enumeration proves that every omitted feasible route has nonnegative reduced cost under its dual solution.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master over \(E\) is solved to optimality.
Reduced costs use every constraint of the full node master.
The enumeration proof covers all routes in \(\mathcal R_v\setminus E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted-master value \(z_E\) equals the full node-master LP optimum.
review_flags: A VRP-specific source for enumeration-based node closure is missing.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Aware Route Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost pricing representation with master cuts included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the route master contain covering rows with dual vector \(\pi\) and valid cuts \(\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\gamma_{jr}x_r\ge b_j\) with dual multipliers \(\mu_j\ge0\). For a minimization master written with this sign convention, the cut-aware reduced cost of route \(r\) is \[\bar c_r=c_r-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_r-\sum_j\mu_j\gamma_{jr}.\] Exact cut-aware pricing minimizes this quantity over the node-feasible route family. It is implementable by the underlying route oracle when every aggregate coefficient \(\gamma_{jr}\) can be accumulated from a finite pricing state or otherwise evaluated exactly during route generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Route pricing must subtract every active cut’s dual-weighted route coefficient; exact integration requires those coefficients to be computable within the pricing oracle.
assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization LP using the displayed inequality and dual-sign convention.
Every active cut has a well-defined coefficient \(\gamma_{jr}\) for each feasible route.
Pricing optimizes over the current node-feasible route family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A route is improving exactly when its cut-aware reduced cost satisfies \(\bar c_r<0\).

notation.meaning: coefficient of route r in cut j

children.title: Robust Cut Integration
children.top_down_role: Integration regimes for cuts whose pricing contributions remain compatible with the route-pricing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing-oracle condition for robust cuts in branch-price-cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a route family generated by a finite-state pricing oracle, a master cut indexed by \(j\) is robustly integrated if its route coefficient admits an additive finite-state representation \[\gamma_{jr}=q_j(s_0)+\sum_{(s,a,s')\in r}g_j(s,a,s')+h_j(s_f),\] or an equivalent exact recursion of fixed state dimension independent of the number of generated columns. Under dual multiplier \(\mu_j\), the term \(-\mu_j\gamma_{jr}\) can then be incorporated into transition and terminal costs without changing the oracle's feasibility state space or asymptotic state dimension. A cut family is robust when every active member satisfies this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is robust when its route coefficient has an exact fixed-dimensional additive recursion, allowing its dual term to enter pricing without enlarging feasibility state.
assumptions_latex: Routes correspond to finite state-transition sequences in the pricing oracle.
Cut coefficients and dual multipliers are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust cuts can be included directly in exact route pricing by modifying transition or terminal costs.

notation.meaning: coefficient of route r in cut j
transition contribution to the cut coefficient

children.title: Nonrobust Cut Integration
children.top_down_role: Integration regimes for cuts requiring additional pricing state, modified costs, or specialized coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrobust Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanism when cut coefficients lack the pricing oracle’s state decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an active master cut have route coefficient \(\gamma_r\) and dual multiplier \(\mu\ne0\). If two partial routes reach the same pricing state but admit continuations for which their incremental values of \(\gamma_r\) differ, then that state is insufficient to compute the cut-aware reduced cost \(\bar c_r=c_r-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_r-\mu\gamma_r\). Treating the cut as though it were additive in the existing state can merge labels having different future reduced costs and may discard the true minimum-reduced-cost route. Exact integration therefore requires augmented state, explicit coefficient evaluation, or another exact mechanism; absent one of these, pricing cannot certify that every omitted route has nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a cut coefficient depends on route history omitted from the pricing state, direct pricing can lose the best route and cannot certify closure without augmentation.
assumptions_latex: The pricing algorithm merges or dominates labels solely through its declared state.
The active cut has nonzero dual multiplier.
The cut coefficient is not determined recursively by that state and subsequent transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unaugmented pricing is not an exact oracle for the cut-modified reduced costs and cannot support a valid no-improving-route certificate.

notation.meaning: route coefficient in the nonrobust cut

children.top_down_role: Compatibility boundaries plus implementation tradeoffs between robust and nonrobust cut classes.

assumptions_latex: The route-pricing subproblem is represented by a state graph whose path costs and resource consumptions are additive over state transitions.
Master cuts enter pricing through their dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cut family is robust precisely while its dual contribution admits an additive representation on the existing pricing state graph; crossing this boundary requires augmenting the state or replacing exact pricing by another valid mechanism.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master cut indexed by \(k\), call its integration robust relative to \(G_s\) if there exist arc values \(d_{ka}\) such that every feasible route represented by a path \(P_r\) satisfies \[\Delta_k(r)=\sum_{a\in P_r}d_{ka},\] and these values can be evaluated without enlarging the state space of \(G_s\). The integration is nonrobust when no such representation exists on that state graph. A cut-robustness transition occurs when adding or activating a cut changes pricing from the first regime to the second, or when a state augmentation restores the first regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Route-Relaxation Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers refinement by progressively excluding routes admitted only by a route relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be the exact feasible-route family and let \(\mathcal R_0\supseteq\mathcal R_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\mathcal R_T=\mathcal R\). For each \(t\), consider the same minimization master formulation restricted to columns from \(\mathcal R_t\), and let \(z(\mathcal R_t)\) denote its optimal value, with value \(+\infty\) if it is infeasible. Then \[z(\mathcal R_0)\le z(\mathcal R_1)\le\cdots\le z(\mathcal R_T)=z(\mathcal R).\] Thus a refinement is valid when it removes only routes outside \(\mathcal R\), and reaching \(\mathcal R_T\) recovers the exact route-master relaxation.

children.title: Core VRP Hardness Consequences
children.top_down_role: Complexity consequences inherited by basic vehicle-routing families.

assumptions_latex: The core VRP class permits the one-vehicle, nonbinding-capacity instances used by the embedding.
The corresponding TSP decision problem is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The core VRP decision problem is NP-hard, and a polynomial-time exact core-VRP algorithm would yield a polynomial-time exact TSP algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States only the exact-computation consequence of the cost-preserving TSP embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f\) maps every TSP instance \(I\) and threshold \(B\) in polynomial time to a core VRP instance \(f(I)\) with the same threshold, such that \(I\) has a Hamiltonian tour of cost at most \(B\) if and only if \(f(I)\) has a feasible routing solution of cost at most \(B\). Then TSP decision polynomially reduces to core VRP decision. Consequently, core VRP decision is NP-hard. In particular, any polynomial-time algorithm computing an optimal solution for every core VRP instance would compute optimal TSP tours in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cost-preserving TSP embedding makes core VRP NP-hard and transfers any general polynomial-time exact VRP algorithm back to TSP.

That embedding proves equivalence only if \(\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal F\) and every solution in \(\mathcal F\) corresponding to the constructed instance maps back to a Hamiltonian tour of equal cost. Such failure invalidates this particular reduction; it does not imply that the restricted variant is tractable.

children.title: Capacity-Induced Hardness
children.top_down_role: Hardness arising from vehicle-capacity restrictions or demand packing.

assumptions_latex: Customers have integral demands and identical vehicle capacity.
Travel costs are zero, so only capacity feasibility matters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fleet-feasibility for this restricted capacitated VRP is strongly NP-hard through a polynomial reduction from 3-PARTITION.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses capacity feasibility alone, with routing costs suppressed, to encode 3-PARTITION.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a 3-PARTITION instance with \(B/4<a_i<B/2\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^{3m}a_i=mB\), create one customer of demand \(a_i\) for each item, provide \(m\) identical vehicles of capacity \(B\), and set every travel cost to zero. A feasible routing assignment exists if and only if the demands can be divided among the vehicles without exceeding capacity. The bounds and total demand force every vehicle to carry exactly three customers totaling \(B\). Hence feasibility is equivalent to 3-PARTITION, yielding strong NP-hardness even though route geometry contributes nothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero travel costs, assigning customer demands to capacity-limited vehicles encodes 3-PARTITION, so capacity feasibility alone makes the restricted VRP strongly NP-hard.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isolates the combinatorial partition of customers between two capacity-limited routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive integers \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\) with even total, construct a VRP having customer demands \(q_i=a_i\), two vehicles, capacity \(Q=\frac12\sum_i a_i\), and zero travel costs. Since total demand equals \(2Q\), a feasible pair of routes exists exactly when the customer set can be partitioned into two subsets, each having total demand \(Q\). The construction and threshold are polynomially encoded, so PARTITION reduces to this feasibility problem. The inherited hardness is weak because the source problem admits pseudopolynomial dynamic programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting demands between two capacity-Q routes exactly represents PARTITION, giving weak NP-hardness even when travel costs vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Induced Hardness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction fits the partition-hardness container, but a source must support weak NP-hardness for the even-total PARTITION restriction and the precise two-vehicle feasibility formulation.

children.title: Capacity–Partition Interaction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where packing structure interacts with route partitioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity–Partition Interaction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates trivial assignment, weak two-way partition, and strong three-item partition regimes within zero-cost capacity feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the zero-cost capacity-feasibility restriction, suppose every customer satisfies \(Q/2<q_i\le Q\). No route can then contain two customers, so feasibility is equivalent to having at least one available vehicle per customer. For instances with two vehicles, capacity \(Q=\tfrac12\sum_i q_i\), and total demand \(2Q\), feasibility expresses the weak PARTITION regime. For instances with \(m\) vehicles, \(Q/4<q_i<Q/2\), and \(\sum_i q_i=mQ\), every feasible route contains exactly three customers totaling \(Q\), giving the strong 3-PARTITION regime. These boundaries concern the permitted demand-grouping structure in this zero-cost restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every demand fits alone but exceeds half a vehicle's capacity, feasibility only checks whether there are enough vehicles; balanced two-way grouping yields the weak PARTITION regime, while forced three-customer grouping yields the strong 3-PARTITION regime.
assumptions_latex: Customer demands \(q_i\) and vehicle capacity \(Q\) are positive integers.
Travel costs are zero, and the number of available vehicles is specified by the instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within this restriction, the grouping regime ranges from trivial singleton assignment to weak two-way partition and strong forced three-item partition.

notation.meaning: number of available vehicles in the 3-PARTITION regime

children.title: Scheduling-Induced VRP Hardness
children.top_down_role: Hardness transferred through sequencing, timing, or service-schedule restrictions.

assumptions_latex: Jobs are nonpreemptive and have release times, deadlines, processing times, and sequence-dependent setup times.
The VRP variant permits one vehicle, service times, time windows, and travel times.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible one-vehicle schedules and feasible time-window routes correspond under the construction, so hardness of the scheduling problem transfers to that VRP variant.

notation.meaning: release time and deadline of job i
setup or travel time from i to j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a one-machine scheduling correspondence for VRP with service times and time windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Map each job \(i\) to a customer with time window \([r_i,d_i]\) and service time \(p_i\), and set travel time from customer \(i\) to customer \(j\) equal to the sequence-dependent setup time \(s_{ij}\). Interpret \(d_i\) as a latest service-completion time, or replace the latest service-start time by \(d_i-p_i\). A vehicle order and its service-start times then form a feasible route exactly when the same order and start times form a feasible nonpreemptive single-machine schedule. The mapping is polynomial and transfers the source scheduling problem's hardness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jobs become customers, processing becomes service, setup becomes travel, and release-deadline constraints become time windows, transferring scheduling hardness to the corresponding VRP.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling-Induced VRP Hardness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scheduling representation fits the container, but the exact correspondence depends on service-start versus completion deadlines and treatment of setup or travel from and to the depot. Those conventions require a source and fuller specification.

children.title: Resource-Induced VRP Hardness
children.top_down_role: Hardness caused by consumable, renewable, or route-level resources.

assumptions_latex: A route must obey an integral resource budget and may collect an additive reward.
The routing graph may be acyclic, and arc resource use and reward are binary-encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resource-constrained route optimization is weakly NP-hard even on an acyclic graph, by reduction from 0-1 knapsack.

notation.meaning: weight and value of item i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isolates hardness of additive resource feasibility in route optimization and pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a 0-1 knapsack instance, construct a layered acyclic graph with one layer per item. Between consecutive layers provide a skip arc of resource use and reward zero and a take arc of resource use \(w_i\) and reward \(v_i\). Every source-to-sink path selects a subset \(S\), consumes \(\sum_{i\in S}w_i\), and earns \(\sum_{i\in S}v_i\). Therefore finding a feasible path of resource consumption at most \(Q\) and reward at least a prescribed threshold is equivalent to knapsack. The resulting resource-constrained route problem is weakly NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A layered route choosing take-or-skip arcs encodes knapsack, making additive resource-constrained route optimization weakly NP-hard even without cyclic routing structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Induced VRP Hardness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record proves hardness of a resource-constrained path problem on a layered DAG, not hardness of a VRP variant. It therefore does not fill the exact terminal container Resource-Induced VRP Hardness, even though it may belong under route pricing or resource-constrained paths.

children.title: Scheduling–Resource Coupling
children.top_down_role: Hardness regimes created by coupled temporal plus resource restrictions.

assumptions_latex: Time-window feasibility and an additive resource budget must both hold along a route.
Partial-route labels record sufficient time and resource state for feasible extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scheduling and resource constraints are coupled through the reachable label set; componentwise dominance is valid only when future feasibility and extension cost are monotone in both recorded resources.

notation.meaning: label with time, resource consumption, and cost
two labels ending at the same pricing state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the label-dominance boundary created by simultaneous scheduling and resource restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For labels \(L_1=(t_1,q_1,c_1)\) and \(L_2=(t_2,q_2,c_2)\) ending at the same state and having identical discrete visit information, discard \(L_2\) under componentwise dominance only if \(t_1\le t_2\), \(q_1\le q_2\), and \(c_1\le c_2\), and every extension feasible from \(L_2\) is feasible from \(L_1\) with no greater extension cost. If waiting rules, replenishment, time-dependent consumption, or other transitions violate this monotonicity, componentwise dominance is not a valid certificate and the state or dominance test must be refined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time and resource states may be pruned componentwise only when every continuation preserves feasibility and cost monotonicity in both dimensions.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling–Resource Coupling

children.title: Strong-Hardness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes retaining hardness under polynomially bounded numerical data.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Hardness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong NP-hardness for integer-encoded decision versions of vehicle-routing subfamilies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be a vehicle-routing decision problem whose instances contain nonnegative integer data, and let \(m(I)\) be the number of combinatorial objects in instance \(I\). The family \(\mathcal{P}\) is strongly NP-hard if there exists a polynomial \(p\) such that the restriction \(\{I: \max_j a_j(I)\le p(m(I))\}\) remains NP-hard, where \(a_j(I)\) ranges over all numerical input values. Equivalently, hardness persists when those values have polynomial magnitude and hence polynomial-length unary encodings. Consequently, a pseudopolynomial exact algorithm for this restricted family would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong hardness means NP-hardness persists even when every numerical datum is polynomially bounded; thus pseudopolynomial exact algorithms are excluded unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{P}\) is a decision problem with binary-encoded nonnegative integer data.
The restricted instances retain polynomial-size combinatorial descriptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{P}\) remains NP-hard under polynomially bounded numerical data.

notation.meaning: Combinatorial size parameter of instance I.
A numerical input value in instance I.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation; Encoding and Time and Space Complexity, pp. 21–23

review_flags: locator supports encoding framework; strong-NP-hardness terminology requires source confirmation

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Complexity, Oracles, and Numerical Computation; Encoding and Time and Space Complexity, pp. 21–23
