intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the indexing permits step k to eject undefined customer u_{k+1}. The permitted intermediate violations and terminal-chain semantics are framework-dependent and require a specific source before correction.

children.title: Variable-Depth Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods whose composite move depth varies during exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Depth Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhoods whose accepted move length is selected during search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N_k(x)\) denote the solutions reachable from \(x\) by an admissible composite move of exactly \(k\) elementary steps. Given a finite search-dependent depth set \(K(x)\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots\}\), the variable-depth neighborhood is \[\mathcal N_{m VD}(x)=\bigcup_{k\in K(x)}\mathcal N_k(x).\] The search may extend or terminate a partial composite move according to its accumulated objective change and feasibility state; hence the selected depth need not be fixed before exploration. Only feasible terminal states belong to \(\mathcal N_{m VD}(x)\), even when the specified scheme permits infeasible intermediate states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-depth neighborhood unions feasible composite moves of several allowed lengths, with the realized length chosen while the move is explored.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal N_k(x)\) is defined by a common admissible elementary-step scheme.
The search-dependent set \(K(x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N_{m VD}(x)=\bigcup_{k\in K(x)}\mathcal N_k(x)\), restricted to feasible terminal states.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the union over a search-dependent depth set is a proposed formalization rather than a uniquely standard definition. A variable-depth-search source must substantiate the adaptive extension and termination semantics.

children.title: Chain Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Feasibility, closure, or truncation boundaries for linked moves.

knowledge_statements.title: Chain Termination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible stopping rules for finite chain-based moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partial chain state \(s_i\) at depth \(i\), a termination regime is a predicate \(T(s_i,i)\). A chain stops at the first index \(i\) for which \(T(s_i,i)=1\). Standard admissible predicates include successful closure, where no object remains displaced and the routing state is feasible; bounded-depth stopping, where \(i=K_{\max}\); dead-end stopping, where no admissible extension exists; and repetition stopping, where the state signature has occurred previously. A solution-producing termination is valid only under successful closure; the other regimes terminate exploration without returning the partial state as a neighbor unless it is independently feasible and closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chain stops on feasible closure, a depth limit, a dead end, or repeated state; only a closed feasible state is automatically returned as a neighbor.
assumptions_latex: Every partial chain state has a well-defined displaced-object status and state signature.
\(K_{\max}\) is a finite positive depth bound when bounded-depth stopping is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A terminal chain state is solution-producing only if it satisfies the regime's closure and feasibility requirements.

notation.meaning: partial chain state at depth i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic finite-search termination predicates for chain neighborhoods
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the asserted catalogue and first-trigger stopping rule combine framework-dependent closure, depth, dead-end, and repetition policies without a source. Their priority and neighbor-producing consequences require documentation.

children.title: Destroy Operators
children.top_down_role: Removal mechanisms that create a partial routing solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Destroy Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial-solution maps used in large-neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be a complete routing solution on customer set \(V\). A destroy operator with removal parameter \(q\) is a possibly randomized map \(D_q\) returning \((p,R)=D_q(x)\), where \(R\subseteq V\), \(|R|=q\), and \(p\) is obtained from \(x\) by deleting exactly the customers in \(R\) and reconnecting each residual route according to the routing representation. Every customer in \(V\setminus R\) retains exactly one assignment in \(p\). The partial state may be evaluated with relaxed constraints, but it records sufficient route and resource information for a repair operator to reinsert all members of \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A destroy operator removes a prescribed number of customers from a complete routing solution and returns the residual routes together with the removed set.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) assigns every customer in the finite set \(V\) exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_q(x)=(p,R)\) has \(|R|=q\), and \(p\) contains exactly the customers in \(V\setminus R\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but removing exactly q customers and retaining the specified resource information describe one destroy-operator convention rather than every LNS destroy operator. A specific LNS source is required.

children.title: Repair Operators
children.top_down_role: Reinsertion mechanisms that reconstruct a complete feasible solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion maps that reinsert customers into partial routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((p,R)\) be a partial routing state whose assigned customers are \(V\setminus R\). A repair operator \(P\) repeatedly selects a customer \(u\in R\) and an allowed insertion position, updates the affected route and resource profiles, and removes \(u\) from \(R\). It returns either a complete feasible solution \(x'=P(p,R)\) after every removed customer has been inserted exactly once, or a distinguished failure value \(\bot\) if its prescribed insertion rule cannot complete the solution. A successful repair satisfies \(V(x')=V\) and every routing constraint of the underlying problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repair operator reinserts every removed customer exactly once and returns a complete feasible routing solution, or reports failure when its insertion rule cannot finish.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) assigns exactly the customers in \(V\setminus R\).
The set of allowed insertion positions and the feasibility tests are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(p,R)\in\mathcal X\cup\{\bot\}\), and any output in \(\mathcal X\) assigns every customer in \(V\) exactly once.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the failure-return convention requires a source, and the conclusion introduces the solution space X without defining it in the statement or notation.

children.title: Removal–Reinsertion Coupling
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between removal patterns plus subsequent reconstruction choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Removal–Reinsertion Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large neighborhoods represented by compatible destroy–repair compositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) and \(\mathcal P\) be families of destroy and repair operators. For a feasible solution \(x\), their coupled large neighborhood is \[\mathcal N_{\mathcal D,\mathcal P}(x)=\{P(D(x)):D\in\mathcal D,\ P\in\mathcal P,\ P(D(x))\ne\bot,\ P(D(x))\text{ is feasible}\}.\] If operators are randomized, the operational neighborhood is the support of this set-valued composition over their random choices. Compatibility requires that the partial-state representation emitted by each selected \(D\) contains every route and resource field consumed by \(P\); otherwise that pair contributes no neighbor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled large neighborhood consists of feasible complete solutions produced by applying a compatible repair operator to a destroyed solution.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D\in\mathcal D\) returns a partial routing state and removed-customer set.
Each \(P\in\mathcal P\) returns a feasible completion or \(\bot\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N_{\mathcal D,\mathcal P}(x)\) is the feasible support of the compositions \(P\circ D\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: large neighborhoods are compositions of destroy and repair maps
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but a source must support this support-of-compositions formulation. The notation also suppresses that D(x) is a partial-state tuple and that randomized P(D(x)) denotes outcomes across random choices.

children.title: Adaptive Operator Selection
children.top_down_role: Search regimes that vary operator choice using observed performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Operator Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based adaptive sampling of destroy–repair operator pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\) be a finite set of destroy–repair pairs and initialize \(w_o^{(0)}>0\) for every \(o\in O\). At iteration \(t\), sample \(o_t\) with \[p_o^{(t)}=\frac{w_o^{(t)}}{\sum_{j\in O}w_j^{(t)}},\] apply \(o_t\) to the incumbent, and assign a bounded score \(s_t\ge0\) from the prescribed outcome categories. At the end of an update period, set \(w_o\leftarrow(1-\rho)w_o+\rho\bar s_o\) for every used operator, where \(0<\rho\le1\) and \(\bar s_o\) is its period-average score; retain unused weights. Stop under the outer search rule and output its incumbent or best-found solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operator pairs are sampled in proportion to positive weights, then their weights are smoothed toward observed outcome scores at periodic updates.
assumptions_latex: \(O\) is finite and all initial weights are positive.
Scores are nonnegative and the reaction factor satisfies \(0<\rho\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every iteration, \(p^{(t)}\) is a probability distribution on \(O\), and weight updates adapt future selection to recorded scores.

notation.meaning: weight of operator pair o at iteration t
selection probability of operator pair o

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical score-and-weight adaptive operator-selection scheme
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the claimed probability distribution can fail: with rho=1 and zero period-average scores, all used weights can become zero and the next normalization may be undefined. The exact adaptive update variant requires a source before choosing the proper positivity safeguard.

children.title: Intra-Route Move Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood structures whose modified elements remain within one route.

knowledge_statements.title: Intra-Route Move Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood moves confined to a single vehicle route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\) be a routing solution. A move is intra-route if there exists an index \(h\) such that every route \(r_j\) with \(j\ne h\) is unchanged and the customer multiset of \(r_h\) is preserved, while its visit sequence is transformed by an allowed operation. For a move family \(M\), \[\mathcal N_M^{\rm intra}(x)=\{x':x'\text{ is feasible and obtained by applying some }\mu\in M\text{ within one }r_h\}.\] Thus the regime changes ordering within one route but neither customer-to-vehicle assignments nor the number of routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intra-route move changes the visit order within exactly one route while preserving every customer assignment and leaving all other routes unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(x=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\) assigns each customer to exactly one route.
Every returned neighbor satisfies the routing constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x'\in\mathcal N_M^{\rm intra}(x)\), all route customer sets equal those of \(x\), and at most one route sequence differs.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard route-scope classification of local-search moves
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the plain statement says exactly one route changes while the formal definition and conclusion allow at most one, including a null transformation. A routing-neighborhood source is needed to settle the intended convention.

children.title: Inter-Route Move Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood structures that transfer or reconnect elements across routes.

knowledge_statements.title: Inter-Route Move Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood moves jointly modifying multiple vehicle routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\) be a routing solution. A move is inter-route if it modifies at least two route sequences through customer transfer, customer exchange, segment exchange, or route reconnection. For an allowed move family \(M\), \[\mathcal N_M^{\rm inter}(x)=\{x':x'\text{ is feasible and obtained by one }\mu\in M\text{ acting on at least two routes}\}.\] Customers remain globally assigned exactly once, but their route assignments may change. Empty-route creation or deletion is permitted only when explicitly allowed by the fleet convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inter-route move jointly changes at least two routes, possibly changing customer-to-route assignments, while preserving global single assignment and feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(x=(r_1,\ldots,r_m)\) assigns each customer exactly once.
The fleet convention specifies whether empty routes may be created or removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(x'\in\mathcal N_M^{\rm inter}(x)\) is feasible, preserves global customer coverage, and differs from \(x\) on at least two routes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard route-scope classification of local-search moves
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits, but the requirement that at least two route sequences differ and the handling of empty-route creation or deletion are convention-dependent and need a vehicle-routing neighborhood source.

children.title: Capacity Feasibility Screening
children.top_down_role: Screening of moves against vehicle or route capacity limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Feasibility Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact route-load screening for capacitated routing moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each customer \(i\) have nonnegative demand \(q_i\), and let vehicle route \(r\) have capacity \(Q_r\). A candidate move producing routes \(r'_1,\ldots,r'_m\) passes capacity screening exactly when \[\sum_{i\in r'_h}q_i\le Q_{r'_h}\qquad\text{for every changed route }r'_h.\] Unchanged routes need not be recomputed if they were feasible before the move. Equivalently, when a changed route has old load \(L_h\), removed set \(A_h\), and inserted set \(B_h\), its new load is \(L'_h=L_h-\sum_{i\in A_h}q_i+\sum_{i\in B_h}q_i\), and the screen requires \(L'_h\le Q_{r'_h}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A move passes capacity screening precisely when each changed route's old load minus removed demand plus inserted demand does not exceed its vehicle capacity.
assumptions_latex: Customer demands satisfy \(q_i\ge0\).
All unchanged routes are capacity-feasible before the move.
Capacity consumption is additive across customers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate move is capacity-feasible if and only if \(L'_h\le Q_{r'_h}\) for every changed route.

notation.meaning: capacity of the vehicle serving route r
load of changed route h after the move

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive capacity feasibility condition for capacitated vehicle routing
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits and the arithmetic is correct for additive deterministic customer demands, but no CVRP source supports the claimed exact screening equivalence or confirms that this restricted capacity model is the intended local scope.

children.title: Load-Profile Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Feasibility over cumulative pickup or delivery loads along a route.

knowledge_statements.title: Load-Profile Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-route capacity feasibility with signed pickup and delivery quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a route \(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m\), let \(q_{v_k}\) be the signed load added at visit \(v_k\), let \(L_0\) be the departure load, and let \(Q\) be vehicle capacity. Define the load profile by \[L_k=L_0+\sum_{h=1}^{k}q_{v_h},\qquad k=1,\ldots,m.\] The route is load-profile feasible exactly when \(0\le L_k\le Q\) for every \(k=0,\ldots,m\), together with any prescribed terminal-load condition such as \(L_m=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A route is feasible when its cumulative signed load remains between zero and vehicle capacity at every visit and satisfies any required terminal load.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\ge 0\) and \(0\le L_0\le Q\).
\(q_{v_k}\in\mathbb{R}\) uses one consistent pickup-positive sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le L_k\le Q\) for all \(k=0,\ldots,m\).

notation.meaning: vehicle load immediately after visit k
signed load change at customer i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no cited source supports the signed-load convention or optional terminal-load condition.

children.title: Residual-Capacity Filters
children.top_down_role: Move rejection or acceptance using remaining route capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Capacity Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact capacity screening when a move’s load-profile increments are known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an incumbent route have loads \(L_k\in[0,Q]\). If a proposed neighborhood move changes the load after position \(k\) by a known increment \(\Delta_k\), its candidate profile is \(L'_k=L_k+\Delta_k\). The residual-capacity filter accepts the move precisely when \[\max_k\{L_k+\Delta_k-Q\}\le 0\quad\text{and}\quad \min_k\{L_k+\Delta_k\}\ge 0.\] Equivalently, every positive increment must not exceed residual capacity \(Q-L_k\), and every negative increment must not exceed the available load \(L_k\) in magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A move passes exactly when every changed route position has enough unused capacity for increases and enough current load for decreases.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le L_k\le Q\) for the incumbent route.
\(\Delta_k\) is the exact move-induced load change at position \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le L_k+\Delta_k\le Q\) at every affected position.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is correct when the increments are exact and fits residual-capacity filtering, but it has no routing-specific source or locator.

children.title: Time-Window Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation of allowable service-time ranges through modified routes.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Window Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward earliest-time and backward latest-time propagation on a fixed route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For route \(v_0,\ldots,v_m\), initialize \(E_0=a_{v_0}\) and propagate earliest service times by \[E_k=\max\{a_{v_k},E_{k-1}+s_{v_{k-1}}+t_{v_{k-1}v_k}\}.\] Initialize \(H_m=b_{v_m}\) and propagate latest service times backward by \[H_k=\min\{b_{v_k},H_{k+1}-s_{v_k}-t_{v_kv_{k+1}}\}.\] Stop and declare infeasibility if \(E_k>H_k\) for some \(k\); otherwise output the feasible service-time intervals \([E_k,H_k]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate earliest times forward and latest times backward; the fixed route is infeasible if any propagated interval becomes empty.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\le b_i\), \(s_i\ge0\), and \(t_{ij}\ge0\).
Waiting before service is allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_k\le H_k\) for every \(k\) certifies nonempty propagated service-time intervals.

notation.meaning: service-start time window at vertex i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward/backward propagation algorithm is coherent for fixed-route hard time windows with waiting, but no supporting source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Schedule Feasibility Screening
children.top_down_role: Screening of candidate moves against route scheduling constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Schedule Feasibility Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-time certificate for fixed-order routing with hard time windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a fixed route \(v_0,\ldots,v_m\), compute \(T_0=a_{v_0}\) and \[T_k=\max\{a_{v_k},T_{k-1}+s_{v_{k-1}}+t_{v_{k-1}v_k}\},\qquad k=1,\ldots,m.\] If \(T_k>b_{v_k}\) at the first violating position, that index certifies infeasibility: every schedule respecting route order and travel times reaches \(v_k\) no earlier than \(T_k\). If no violation occurs, \((T_0,\ldots,T_m)\) is itself a feasible earliest-start schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The earliest-start recursion either constructs a feasible schedule or returns the first late visit as an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\le b_i\), \(s_i\ge0\), and \(t_{ij}\ge0\).
Arbitrary nonnegative waiting is permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(T_k\le b_{v_k}\) for all \(k\), or the first index with \(T_k>b_{v_k}\) certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: earliest service start at route position k

children.title: Waiting-Time Effects
children.top_down_role: Impact of waiting slack on the feasibility of route modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Waiting-Time Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of early arrival when waiting is allowed under hard time windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose service at \(v_k\) may start within \([a_{v_k},b_{v_k}]\), and let arrival be \(A_k\). The earliest feasible service start and induced waiting are \[T_k=\max\{A_k,a_{v_k}\},\qquad W_k=\max\{0,a_{v_k}-A_k\}.\] Hence arriving before \(a_{v_k}\) does not violate the window; it adds waiting and yields departure time \(D_k=T_k+s_{v_k}\). An arrival violates the hard window exactly when \(A_k>b_{v_k}\), because waiting cannot repair lateness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Early arrival creates waiting rather than infeasibility, while arrival after the latest service time is irreparable.
assumptions_latex: \(a_{v_k}\le b_{v_k}\) and \(s_{v_k}\ge0\).
Waiting is allowed without an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k\le b_{v_k}\) is locally feasible, with \(W_k=\max\{0,a_{v_k}-A_k\}\).

notation.meaning: arrival time at route position k

children.title: Precedence Feasibility Filters
children.top_down_role: Move screening for pickup–delivery or service-order requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Precedence Feasibility Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient position test for fixed-route precedence constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq V\times V\) be required precedence pairs, where \((i,j)\in P\) means that visit \(i\) must occur before visit \(j\) on the same route. For candidate route \(r\), with position map \(\pi_r\), the precedence filter accepts exactly when \[\pi_r(i)<\pi_r(j)\qquad\text{for every }(i,j)\in P.\] In pickup-and-delivery routing, each request pair \((p_h,d_h)\) additionally requires both vertices to belong to the same route; failure of either test rejects the candidate move.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate passes when every required predecessor occurs earlier than its successor, with paired pickup and delivery on the same route when required.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) visits every constrained vertex at most once.
\(P\) specifies strict within-route precedence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_r(i)<\pi_r(j)\) for all applicable \((i,j)\in P\).

notation.meaning: position of vertex i in route r
pickup and delivery of request h

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The position test is appropriate as a precedence-feasibility condition, including same-route pairing for pickup-and-delivery requests, but no source identifies the intended routing variant.

children.title: Energy Feasibility Filters
children.top_down_role: Move screening for battery, fuel, or refueling limitations.

knowledge_statements.title: Energy Feasibility Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Battery-state screening for a fixed route with prescribed replenishment amounts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For route \(v_0,\ldots,v_m\), let \(e_k\ge0\) be energy consumed from \(v_{k-1}\) to \(v_k\), let \(r_k\ge0\) be energy replenished at \(v_k\), and let battery capacity be \(B\). Starting from \(b_0\in[0,B]\), define arrival energy \(b_k^-=b_{k-1}-e_k\) and departure energy \(b_k=\min\{B,b_k^-+r_k\}\). The candidate passes the energy filter exactly when \(b_k^-\ge0\) for every \(k=1,\ldots,m\); otherwise the first negative arrival state certifies energy infeasibility under the prescribed replenishment plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate battery charge along the route and reject when any leg requires more energy than is available at its departure.
assumptions_latex: Energy consumptions and replenishment amounts are fixed for the candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_k^-\ge0\) for every traversed leg.

notation.meaning: battery energy upon arrival at position k

children.title: Loading Feasibility Filters
children.top_down_role: Move screening for loading order, compartment, or handling restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Loading Feasibility Filters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe aggregate screening for multidimensional vehicle-loading constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let items assigned to a vehicle be \(I\). For each resource dimension \(d=1,\ldots,p\), item \(i\) consumes \(w_{id}\ge0\) and the vehicle provides capacity \(Q_d\). The aggregate loading filter rejects the assignment whenever \[\sum_{i\in I}w_{id}>Q_d\quad\text{for some }d.\] Passing all inequalities is necessary but need not be sufficient for geometric packing, stacking, accessibility, or incompatibility constraints. Thus a rejection is a valid infeasibility certificate, whereas an accepted assignment requires any remaining loading constraints to be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exceeding any aggregate loading capacity safely rejects an assignment, but passing aggregate tests does not guarantee physical packability.
assumptions_latex: \(w_{id}\ge0\) and \(Q_d\ge0\).
Each item assigned to the vehicle contributes to every applicable capacity dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in I}w_{id}\le Q_d\) for every \(d\) is necessary for loading feasibility.

children.title: Coupled Resource Screening
children.top_down_role: Joint feasibility treatment when multiple route resources interact.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Resource Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint feasibility screening through route-state transition maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^p\) collect all resource states after route position \(k\), and let the candidate route induce transitions \(x_k=F_k(x_{k-1})\). Let \(X_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) encode the joint admissible states, including cross-resource constraints. Starting from \(x_0\in X_0\), coupled screening accepts exactly when \[x_k=F_k\circ F_{k-1}\circ\cdots\circ F_1(x_0)\in X_k\qquad(k=1,\ldots,m).\] Testing only coordinatewise bounds is insufficient whenever \(X_k\) is not a Cartesian product or one resource transition depends on another resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate the full resource vector and test joint admissibility; separate scalar checks can miss violations caused by cross-resource dependence.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_k\) is the specified deterministic transition for the candidate route.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\in X_k\) for every route position \(k\).

notation.meaning: joint resource state after position k

children.title: Tabu Search Memory
children.top_down_role: Recency, frequency, or attribute memory in routing search.

knowledge_statements.title: Tabu Search Memory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-term attribute memory with tenure and aspiration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial solution \(x_0\), neighborhood \(N\), objective \(f\), tenure \(\tau\), and incumbent best \(x^*\), initialize tabu expiration times \(T(a)=0\). At iteration \(t\), select a best candidate \(y\in N(x_t)\) whose introduced attributes satisfy \(T(a)\le t\), unless aspiration holds, for example \(f(y)<f(x^*)\). Set \(x_{t+1}=y\), assign \(T(a)=t+\tau\) to attributes whose immediate reversal is forbidden, and update \(x^*\) if improved. Stop under the prescribed iteration or time limit and return \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tabu search records recently changed attributes, temporarily forbids reversing them, permits aspirational improvements, and returns the best solution encountered.
assumptions_latex: \(N(x)\) is finite for every visited solution.
The objective is minimized and \(\tau\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x_s):0\le s\le t\}\) after iteration \(t\).

notation.meaning: tabu expiration iteration of attribute a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the tabu-memory leaf, but the attribute convention, tenure update, aspiration rule, and candidate-selection variant require an authoritative source.

children.title: Guided Local-Search Penalties
children.top_down_role: Penalty-based modification of routing-search preferences.

knowledge_statements.title: Guided Local-Search Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical guided local search using feature utilities and adaptive penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)\) be minimized, with feature indicators \(I_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\), costs \(c_i>0\), penalties \(p_i=0\), and \(\lambda>0\). Repeatedly obtain a local minimum of \[h(x)=f(x)+\lambda\sum_i p_iI_i(x).\] At that solution compute utilities \(u_i=I_i(x)c_i/(1+p_i)\), increase \(p_i\) by one for every feature attaining \(\max_j u_j\), and restart local search from the current solution under the updated augmented objective. Stop by a prescribed budget and return the best solution measured by \(f\), not necessarily by \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Guided local search repeatedly penalizes active high-cost, low-penalty features and optimizes the resulting augmented objective while retaining the best original objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(c_i>0\), \(p_i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\), and \(\lambda>0\).
The feature family is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i\leftarrow p_i+1\) for active features of maximum utility.

notation.meaning: indicator that feature i occurs in solution x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the usual guided-local-search pattern and fits the leaf, but the augmented objective and utility update have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Intensification–Diversification Balance
children.top_down_role: Balance between focused exploitation plus broader trajectory exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Intensification–Diversification Balance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized tradeoff between objective quality and search novelty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)\) be the objective of candidate \(y\), and let \(n(y;M)\ge0\) measure novelty relative to search memory \(M\), with larger values indicating less explored structure. For normalized quantities \(\widehat f\) and \(\widehat n\), a memory-guided minimization rule may select \[y_\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in N(x)}\bigl(\alpha\widehat f(y)-(1-\alpha)\widehat n(y;M)\bigr),\qquad 0\le\alpha\le1.\] Increasing \(\alpha\) favors intensification through objective quality; decreasing it favors diversification through novelty. The endpoint \(\alpha=1\) ignores novelty, while \(\alpha=0\) ignores objective quality in candidate selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted selection score makes the exploitation–exploration tradeoff explicit: larger weight favors objective improvement, while smaller weight favors novel search regions.
assumptions_latex: \(N(x)\) is finite and nonempty.
\(\widehat f\) and \(\widehat n\) use compatible finite normalizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\) continuously controls the stated quality–novelty selection tradeoff.

notation.meaning: novelty of candidate y relative to memory

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the leaf, but the proposed weighted scalarization is an illustrative design rather than a source-supported canonical characterization of intensification–diversification balance.

children.title: Iterated Local Search
children.top_down_role: Routing search based on repeated perturbation followed by local improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterated Local Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical finite-space iterated local search with perturbation, local descent, and incumbent acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite feasible routing set \(S\), objective \(f:S\to\mathbb R\) to minimize, local-search map \(L:S\to S\), perturbation kernel \(P(\cdot\mid x)\), and acceptance rule \(A:S\times S\to S\), initialize \(x=L(x^0)\) and \(x^\star=x\). At iteration \(t\), sample \(y\sim P(\cdot\mid x)\), set \(z=L(y)\), update \(x\leftarrow A(x,z)\), and replace \(x^\star\leftarrow x\) whenever \(f(x)<f(x^\star)\). Stop under a specified iteration, time, or stagnation limit and return \(x^\star\). The map \(L\) must return a solution locally optimal in its declared routing neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly perturb a locally optimal route, improve the perturbed route by local search, apply an acceptance rule, and return the best feasible solution encountered.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and nonempty.
\(L(x)\in S\) and \(f(L(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in S\) is the best solution visited before termination.

notation.meaning: perturbation distribution based at the current solution

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Iterated Local Search leaf, and the finite-space perturbation, local-search, acceptance, and best-so-far structure is mathematically coherent. However, no source reference or inspectable locator is supplied, so the claimed canonical formulation and the requirement that L always return a local optimum cannot be reviewed against evidence.

children.title: Variable-Neighborhood Search
children.top_down_role: Routing search that changes neighborhood structures during exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic variable-neighborhood search with ordered shaking neighborhoods and local improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite feasible routing set, let \(f:S\to\mathbb R\) be minimized, and let \(N_1,\ldots,N_K\) be neighborhoods. Initialize \(x\in S\), \(x^\star=x\), and \(k=1\). Sample a shaken solution \(y\in N_k(x)\cap S\), apply local search to obtain \(z=L(y)\), and, if \(f(z)<f(x)\), set \(x=z\), update \(x^\star\) if necessary, and reset \(k=1\); otherwise set \(k=k+1\). After \(k>K\), restart at \(k=1\) unless the prescribed stopping rule holds. Return \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search increasingly different neighborhoods; after improvement, return to the first neighborhood, and otherwise advance until termination.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and nonempty.
Each invoked set \(N_k(x)\cap S\) is nonempty or has a specified skip rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in S\) is the least-cost solution observed during the search.

notation.meaning: the kth neighborhood of solution x

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Variable-Neighborhood Search leaf, and the ordered shaking, improvement, and neighborhood-index reset scheme is a recognizable basic VNS variant. No source or specific locator is supplied, so the exact restart convention and variant-level formulation remain unsupported.

children.title: Perturbation–Neighborhood Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction between trajectory perturbations plus local neighborhood choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation–Neighborhood Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition linking diversification moves to the basin structure induced by local search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:S\to S\) be a local-search map and define the basin of a local optimum \(u\) by \(B(u)=\{x\in S:L(x)=u\}\). A perturbation kernel \(P(\cdot\mid u)\) and \(L\) are escape-coupled at \(u\) when \(P(S\setminus B(u)\mid u)>0\). They are globally escape-coupled when this inequality holds for every non-global local optimum \(u\). Under repeated independent perturbation trials at such a point, the probability of never leaving its basin after \(m\) trials is at most \((1-p_u)^m\), where \(p_u=P(S\setminus B(u)\mid u)>0\), and hence tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perturbation is coupled effectively to local search when it can leave every nonglobal local optimum’s attraction basin; repeated trials then escape almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
Perturbation trials at a fixed \(u\) are conditionally independent with escape probability at least \(p_u>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{m\to\infty}(1-p_u)^m=0\), so eventual escape from \(B(u)\) has probability one.

notation.meaning: local-search basin of local optimum u

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary basin-escape formulation of perturbation coupling
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the coupling leaf, and the conditional-independent escape calculation is internally coherent. The proposed term "escape-coupled" and its basin-based definition appear record-specific rather than established taxonomy-neutral terminology; without a source and locator, it is unclear whether this is a recognized perturbation-neighborhood coupling principle or a newly coined sufficient condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Large-Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destroy–repair search with online adaptation of operator-selection probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^0\in S\), destroy operators \(D_1,\ldots,D_p\), repair operators \(R_1,\ldots,R_q\), and positive weights \(w^D,w^R\), set \(x=x^0\) and \(x^\star=x^0\). At iteration \(t\), sample \(i\) and \(j\) with probabilities proportional to their weights, form \(y=R_j(D_i(x))\in S\), accept or reject \(y\) by a declared rule, and update \(x^\star\) whenever a lower-cost solution is found. Assign the selected operators a prescribed score \(s_t\), then update each selected weight by \(w\leftarrow(1-\rho)w+\rho s_t\), with \(0<\rho\le1\). Return \(x^\star\) at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly destroy and repair routes while adapting operator-selection weights from observed performance; retain the best feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: Every repair operation returns a member of \(S\).
Initial operator weights are strictly positive.
Scores and the reaction parameter preserve nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in S\) is the best solution generated before the stopping rule fires.

notation.meaning: destroy operator removing part of a routing solution

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Adaptive Large-Neighborhood Search. Destroy-repair iteration and adaptive operator selection are appropriate, but the per-iteration exponential weight update is only one possible adaptation scheme and differs from common segment-based scoring formulations. A source with a precise section, equation, or algorithm locator is required to establish this variant.

children.title: Genetic Routing Search
children.top_down_role: Population-based routing search centered on selection, recombination, or mutation.

knowledge_statements.title: Genetic Routing Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population-based evolutionary search over feasible or decodable routing chromosomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a chromosome space with decoder \(d:G\to S\) and fitness \(F(g)=f(d(g))\) for minimization. Initialize a finite population \(P_0\subseteq G\). At generation \(t\), select parent pairs from \(P_t\), apply a routing recombination operator \(C\), mutate offspring using \(M\), and evaluate their decoded solutions. Form \(P_{t+1}\) from parents and offspring using a declared survivor rule, optionally preserving a chromosome attaining the smallest fitness seen so far. Stop under a prescribed generation, time, or stagnation limit and return the decoded best-so-far chromosome.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evolve a population of route encodings through selection, recombination, mutation, decoding, and survivor selection, then return the best decoded route.
assumptions_latex: \(d(g)\in S\) for every chromosome admitted to a population.
Every population is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(g^\star)\in S\) and \(F(g^\star)\le F(g)\) for every evaluated chromosome \(g\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic genetic-search template specialized to routing
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Genetic Routing Search, and the population, selection, recombination, mutation, decoding, and survivor stages match the leaf. The conclusion quantifies over every evaluated chromosome, but the procedure says best-so-far preservation is optional and does not explicitly define or update g-star independently of the population. No source or locator is supplied to resolve the intended algorithm and tracking convention.

children.title: Memetic Routing Search
children.top_down_role: Population search enhanced by individual-level route improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Memetic Routing Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evolutionary routing search in which offspring undergo explicit local improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use a chromosome space \(G\), decoder \(d:G\to S\), population \(P_t\), recombination \(C\), mutation \(M\), and routing local-search map \(L:S\to S\). For every selected parent pair, generate an offspring chromosome \(g=C(g_1,g_2)\), mutate it, decode \(x=d(M(g))\), and compute \(x'=L(x)\). Insert an encoding of \(x'\) into the candidate population, then apply a declared survivor rule, possibly using both objective value and diversity. Preserve the best solution encountered, stop under a prescribed resource limit, and return that solution. Local improvement is therefore part of offspring evaluation rather than a separate postprocessing step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Create evolutionary offspring, improve every decoded child by routing local search, select survivors, and return the best improved solution.
assumptions_latex: The decoder and local-search map return feasible solutions in \(S\).
Improved solutions can be represented or stored with their chromosomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in S\) is the best locally improved solution observed before termination.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Memetic Routing Search, and explicit local improvement of decoded offspring is a valid memetic architecture. Requiring improvement for every offspring and characterizing it as part of offspring evaluation selects a particular variant rather than the entire family. A cited source with a specific locator is needed.

children.title: Recombination Structures
children.top_down_role: Route, edge, sequence, or assignment structures preserved during recombination.

knowledge_statements.title: Recombination Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving recombination of route components inherited from two parent solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a feasible routing set and let \(E(x)\) denote the route edges or arcs of \(x\in S\). A routing recombination structure is a possibly randomized map \(C:S\times S\to S\) together with an inheritance predicate. It is edge-inheriting when every offspring \(z=C(x,y)\) satisfies \(E(z)\subseteq E(x)\cup E(y)\); it is common-edge preserving when additionally \(E(x)\cap E(y)\subseteq E(z)\). More general route-segment recombination replaces edges by declared contiguous customer subsequences. Any completion step must preserve customer coverage, vehicle capacities, and every other constraint defining \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A routing recombination structure builds a feasible child from parental edges or route segments under an explicit inheritance rule.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is the declared feasible set for the routing instance.
\(E(x)\) uses one fixed directed or undirected edge convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(x,y)\in S\) for all \((x,y)\in S\times S\), with the stated inheritance inclusions when applicable.

notation.meaning: edge or arc set of routing solution x

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind is plausible for Recombination Structures, and the edge-inheritance inclusions are well formed. However, they describe particular edge-inheriting and common-edge-preserving crossover properties rather than a generally accepted definition of every routing recombination structure. The terminology and coverage/capacity completion requirements need an authoritative source and precise locator.

children.title: Local-Improvement Embedding
children.top_down_role: Placement of neighborhood improvement within population-search lifecycles.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Improvement Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Insertion of a monotone local-search stage into offspring production.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:G\to S\) be the offspring decoding-and-repair map and let \(L:S\to S\) be a local-search map satisfying \(f(L(x))\le f(x)\). For every generated chromosome \(g\), compute \(x=Q(g)\), then \(x'=L(x)\), and use \(x'\), rather than \(x\), for fitness evaluation and survivor selection. If the representation is not uniquely determined by a solution, apply a prescribed encoding map \(e:S\to G\) before reinsertion. The embedded stage terminates when its declared neighborhood contains no improving move or when its local resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decode each offspring, locally improve it before evaluation, and re-encode it if the population representation requires chromosomes.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(g)\in S\) for every generated chromosome \(g\).
\(L(x)\in S\) and \(f(L(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x'=L(Q(g))\in S\) and \(f(x')\le f(Q(g))\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Local-Improvement Embedding, and the composition L(Q(g)) correctly captures pre-evaluation improvement. The final sentence allows termination at a local resource limit, in which case the result need not be locally optimal despite the phrase "local-improvement map"; only monotonicity is actually assumed. A source and locator are needed to determine the intended embedding and termination guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Genetic Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Routing genetic search combining repair, local improvement, and diversity-aware survivor selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a population \(P_t\) of routing individuals, each decoded to a feasible solution in \(S\). Select parents, recombine and mutate them, repair the resulting individual if necessary, and apply local search \(L\). Evaluate an improved offspring \(x\) by objective value \(f(x)\) and a diversity score \(\delta(x,P_t)\). Insert \(x\), then, whenever the population exceeds its size bound, remove an individual by a declared survivor ranking that combines quality and diversity while preserving a best-so-far individual. Optionally restart or diversify after stagnation. Stop under a prescribed resource limit and return the least-cost feasible solution encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine genetic variation, feasibility repair, local search, and diversity-aware population management while preserving the best route found.
assumptions_latex: Repair and local search produce members of \(S\).
The survivor rule maintains a finite nonempty population.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in S\) and \(f(x^\star)\le f(x)\) for every generated feasible solution \(x\).

notation.meaning: diversity contribution of x relative to the population

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

Since these mechanisms and survivor rankings are variant-dependent, a specific authoritative source and algorithm or section locator are required.

children.title: Elite-Set Management
children.top_down_role: Selection, retention, or replacement policies for high-quality routing solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Elite-Set Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded archive update balancing objective quality and pairwise separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq S\) be an elite archive of capacity \(m\), let \(d:S\times S\to\mathbb R_+\) measure solution dissimilarity, and let \(\Delta>0\) be a separation threshold. For a candidate \(x\in S\), reject \(x\) if some \(y\in E\) has \(d(x,y)<\Delta\) and \(f(y)\le f(x)\); otherwise remove every such dominated near-duplicate \(y\), insert \(x\), and, if \(|E|>m\), delete a non-best member minimizing a declared quality-diversity ranking. The archive must retain a minimum-cost solution seen so far. Initialize with \(E=\varnothing\) and apply this update to each candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a bounded elite archive by rejecting dominated near-duplicates, admitting useful candidates, and preserving the best solution.
assumptions_latex: Every submitted candidate belongs to \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|E|\le m\), and \(E\) contains a best-cost candidate seen so far.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Elite-Set Management, and the proposed update preserves capacity and a best-so-far member if implemented as stated. The near-duplicate threshold, dominance rule, bulk removal, and quality-diversity deletion policy constitute one particular archive design rather than a canonical definition. No supporting source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Path-Relinking Trajectories
children.top_down_role: Search trajectories connecting selected routing solutions in solution space.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Relinking Trajectories
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy trajectory from an initiating solution toward attributes of a guiding solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a feasible routing set, let \(a:S\to2^{\mathcal A}\) map a solution to its attributes, and choose initiating and guiding solutions \(x^I,x^G\in S\). Set \(x_0=x^I\). While \(a(x_k)\ne a(x^G)\), form the feasible candidate set \(C_k\) of moves that add at least one missing guiding attribute or remove at least one conflicting attribute. Choose \(x_{k+1}\in C_k\) by a declared evaluation rule, record the best solution on the trajectory, and continue until the guide is reached or \(C_k=\varnothing\). Return the best recorded trajectory solution, optionally after local improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move from an initiating route toward a guiding route by progressively incorporating guiding attributes, retaining the best intermediate solution.
assumptions_latex: \(x^I,x^G\in S\).
Every accepted intermediate solution belongs to \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\{x_0,\ldots,x_T\}\subseteq S\) minimizes \(f\) over the generated trajectory.

notation.meaning: attribute set of routing solution x

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
